Whimbrel much larger. Upland Sandpiper similar
but has shorter bill.
Little_Curlew.Best Ways to Identify:
Small size for a curlew with short slightly curved
bill. Grassland habitat preference. Rare
vagrant on Pacific coast.

Little_Egret.Description:
Small white egret, black bill, black legs, yellow
feet. Two long white plumes on nape
in breeding. About 22 inches.
Little_Egret.Behavior:
Wades actively for fish using yellow feet to disturb
prey. Rare but increasing vagrant
to Atlantic coast.
Little_Egret.Habitat:
Coastal marshes and estuaries of Europe and Asia.
Increasingly rare vagrant to Atlantic
coast of North America.
Little_Egret.Similar Looking Birds:
Snowy Egret has yellow feet and black bill. Little
Egret larger with distinctive nape plumes.
Little_Egret.Best Ways to Identify:
Yellow feet on black legs. Black bill. Rare
European vagrant. Nearly identical to
Snowy Egret but slightly larger.

Little_Gull.Description:
Tiny gull, world's smallest. Breeding adult has
black hood, dark red bill, rounded wings with
dark underwing. About 11 inches.
Little_Gull.Behavior:
Dips gracefully to water surface for food. Regular
but uncommon visitor to Great Lakes and Atlantic
coast from Eurasia.
Little_Gull.Habitat:
Breeds in Eurasian marshes. Winters on European
and North American coasts. Regular visitor
to Great Lakes and Atlantic.
Little_Gull.Similar Looking Birds:
Bonaparte's Gull larger. Little Gull tiny with round
wings and dark underwing.
Little_Gull.Best Ways to Identify:
Tiny size and round wings. Dark underwing coverts
distinctive in flight. Black hood
in breeding.

Little_Ringed_Plover.Description:
Small plover. Brown above, white below, black breast
band and head pattern, yellow eye ring, dull
flesh-pink legs. About 6 inches.
Little_Ringed_Plover.Behavior:
Feeds on invertebrates along freshwater margins. Rare
vagrant to western Alaska and Atlantic coast
from Eurasia.
Little_Ringed_Plover.Habitat:
Breeds along freshwater rivers, streams, and gravel
pits across Eurasia. Rare vagrant
to North America.
Little_Ringed_Plover.Similar Looking Birds:
Common Ringed Plover similar. Little Ringed has
yellow eye ring and lacks wing bar.
Little_Ringed_Plover.Best Ways to Identify:
Yellow orbital eye ring diagnostic. Lacks wing bar
visible in flight. Fresh water habitat
preference. Rare vagrant.

Little_Stint.Description:
Very small sandpiper. Breeding adult has rufous
face and breast with white V on back. Non-
breeding gray-brown. About 6 inches.
Little_Stint.Behavior:
Forages actively on mudflats picking small invertebrates.
Rare vagrant to both coasts from Eurasia.
Little_Stint.Habitat:
Breeds on Arctic Eurasian tundra. Winters on African
and South Asian coasts. Rare vagrant to
both coasts of North America.
Little_Stint.Similar Looking Birds:
Semipalmated and Least Sandpipers nearly identical
in non-breeding. Rufous tones in breeding.
Little_Stint.Best Ways to Identify:
Rufous-orange face and back in breeding plumage
with white V. Very small. Rare
vagrant from Eurasia.

Little_Tern.Description:
Tiny tern. White with gray back, black cap with
white forehead, yellow bill with black tip. Small
and fast-flying. About 9 inches.
Little_Tern.Behavior:
Hovers and dives for small fish. Breeds on sandy
beaches. Rare vagrant to North America from
Eurasia.
Little_Tern.Habitat:
Sandy beaches and coastal areas of Eurasia and Africa.
Rare vagrant to Pacific coast
of North America.
Little_Tern.Similar Looking Birds:
Least Tern nearly identical. Little Tern very similar;
different range.
Little_Tern.Best Ways to Identify:
Tiny size. Yellow bill with black tip. White
forehead. Rare vagrant; nearly identical
to Least Tern.

Little_White-Tern.Description:
Small pure white tern, smaller than White Tern.
All white with black-tipped bill, large black
eye. About 9 inches.
Little_White-Tern.Behavior:
Lays single egg on bare branch. Picks fish from
surface. Found on Pacific tropical islands
and atolls.
Little_White-Tern.Habitat:
Tropical Pacific islands including Hawaiian Northwestern
chain and other atolls.
Little_White-Tern.Similar Looking Birds:
White (Fairy) Tern similar but larger. Little White-
Tern smaller with different bill.
Little_White-Tern.Best Ways to Identify:
All-white plumage. Smaller than Fairy Tern. Found
on tropical Pacific islands and
Hawaiian atolls.

Loggerhead_Kingbird.Description:
Large kingbird, black and white head with large head
and bill, white below, brown-black
above. About 9 inches.
Loggerhead_Kingbird.Behavior:
Caribbean island kingbird. Rare vagrant to southern
Florida from Cuba and Bahamas.
Loggerhead_Kingbird.Habitat:
Forest and open areas of Caribbean islands. Rare vagrant
to southern Florida.
Loggerhead_Kingbird.Similar Looking Birds:
Eastern Kingbird similar but smaller-headed. Loggerhead
has noticeably large head.
Loggerhead_Kingbird.Best Ways to Identify:
Large head and heavy bill on kingbird. Black above,
white below. Caribbean species,
rare Florida vagrant.

Loggerhead_Shrike.Description: Gray bird with black mask, hooked bill, and black-and-white wings. Impales prey on thorns.
Loggerhead_Shrike.Behavior: Perches on wires and fence posts. Impales insects, lizards, and small birds on thorns.
Loggerhead_Shrike.Habitat: Open fields, shrubby grasslands, and agricultural areas across North America.
Loggerhead_Shrike.Similar Looking Birds: Northern Mockingbird is larger without black mask; Northern Shrike has barred breast.
Loggerhead_Shrike.Best Ways to Identify: Black mask, hooked bill, and habit of impaling prey on thorns or barbed wire.

Long-billed_Curlew.Description: Large shorebird with extremely long downcurved bill, cinnamon-brown plumage, and barred underparts.
Long-billed_Curlew.Behavior: Probes deeply in mud for crabs and invertebrates with its remarkably long bill.
Long-billed_Curlew.Habitat: Grasslands in breeding season; coastal mudflats and marshes in winter.
Long-billed_Curlew.Similar Looking Birds: Whimbrel is similar but smaller with shorter bill and striped head.
Long-billed_Curlew.Best Ways to Identify: Largest North American shorebird -- extraordinarily long downcurved bill is unmistakable.

Long-billed_Dowitcher.Description: Medium-large shorebird with long bill, rusty-red breeding plumage, and white wedge up the back.
Long-billed_Dowitcher.Behavior: Probes in rapid sewing-machine motion in shallow water. High keek call.
Long-billed_Dowitcher.Habitat: Freshwater marshes and mudflats during migration across North America.
Long-billed_Dowitcher.Similar Looking Birds: Short-billed Dowitcher prefers saltwater; Long-billed prefers freshwater; calls differ.
Long-billed_Dowitcher.Best Ways to Identify: High keek call and freshwater preference separates it from Short-billed Dowitcher.

Long-billed_Murrelet.Description:
Medium alcid. Brown streaked breeding plumage, black
and white winter plumage. Longer bill than Marbled
Murrelet. About 11 inches.
Long-billed_Murrelet.Behavior:
Nests in old-growth forests, sometimes far from sea.
Rare vagrant to North America from Asia. Dives
for fish.
Long-billed_Murrelet.Habitat:
Old-growth forests and coastal waters of East Asia
(Russia, Japan). Rare vagrant to Pacific coast
of North America.
Long-billed_Murrelet.Similar Looking Birds:
Marbled Murrelet nearly identical. Long-billed has
longer bill and less distinct collar.
Long-billed_Murrelet.Best Ways to Identify:
Longer bill than Marbled Murrelet. Different white
collar pattern in winter. Rare Asian
vagrant on Pacific coast.

Long-billed_Thrasher.Description:
Large thrasher, brown above with heavily streaked
white breast, orange eye, long
decurved bill. About 12 inches.
Long-billed_Thrasher.Behavior:
Forages on ground by tossing leaves and debris.
Loud, rich song. Resident in
dense Texas brush country.
Long-billed_Thrasher.Habitat:
Dense thorn scrub and brushy woodland of the
Rio Grande Valley and south
Texas.
Long-billed_Thrasher.Similar Looking Birds:
Brown Thrasher very similar but has yellow eye
and two wing bars. Overlaps
rarely.
Long-billed_Thrasher.Best Ways to Identify:
Orange eye, long decurved bill, heavily streaked
below. Rio Grande Valley brush
country. Similar to Brown Thrasher.

Long-eared_Owl.Description: Medium owl with long ear tufts close together, orange facial disc, and streaked underparts.
Long-eared_Owl.Behavior: Roosts communally in dense conifers during winter. Silent hunter over open fields.
Long-eared_Owl.Habitat: Open country near woodland edges; uses abandoned hawk nests for breeding.
Long-eared_Owl.Similar Looking Birds: Great Horned Owl is larger with wider-set ear tufts; Short-eared has shorter ear tufts.
Long-eared_Owl.Best Ways to Identify: Long ear tufts set close together on an orange facial disc; communal winter roosts.

Long-legged_Buzzard.Description:
Large buteo, pale morph tawny-brown with pale head,
dark carpal patches; dark morph all
dark. About 24 inches.
Long-legged_Buzzard.Behavior:
Hunts small mammals over open steppe. Old World counterpart
to Ferruginous Hawk. Very rare
vagrant to North America.
Long-legged_Buzzard.Habitat:
Open steppe and desert of Europe and Asia. Very rare
vagrant to Atlantic coast
of North America.
Long-legged_Buzzard.Similar Looking Birds:
Ferruginous Hawk similar. Long-legged Buzzard has pale
tail and different underwing pattern.
Long-legged_Buzzard.Best Ways to Identify:
Large pale buteo with pale tail and dark carpal patches.
Old World species, very rare
vagrant.

Long-tailed_Duck.Description: Sea duck. Male has long tail pins, black-and-white winter plumage, and bubbly ow-owdle-ow call.
Long-tailed_Duck.Behavior: Dives deeply -- to 200 feet -- for mollusks in Arctic seas. Very vocal.
Long-tailed_Duck.Habitat: Arctic and subarctic seas; winters on open ocean and large lakes.
Long-tailed_Duck.Similar Looking Birds: No other sea duck has long tail pins and bold black-and-white winter plumage.
Long-tailed_Duck.Best Ways to Identify: Long tail pins on male, black-and-white winter plumage, and yodeling call.

Long-tailed_Jaeger.Description:
Smallest and most elegant jaeger. Very long central
tail feathers, gray back, dark wings without
white flash. About 22 inches including tail.
Long-tailed_Jaeger.Behavior:
Graceful buoyant flight. Less piratical than other
jaegers; forages more independently. Regular offshore
migrant on both coasts.
Long-tailed_Jaeger.Habitat:
Breeds on Arctic tundra. Pelagic outside breeding.
Migrates offshore on both coasts.
Long-tailed_Jaeger.Similar Looking Birds:
Parasitic Jaeger shorter tailed. Long-tailed has very
long streamers and paler gray back.
Long-tailed_Jaeger.Best Ways to Identify:
Very long elegant tail streamers. Pale gray back
without white wing flash. Buoyant graceful
flight.

Long-toed_Stint.Description:
Very small sandpiper. Brown streaked upperparts,
white underparts with streaked breast, long toes,
yellow legs. About 6 inches.
Long-toed_Stint.Behavior:
Walks on floating vegetation using long toes. Forages
in freshwater marshes. Rare vagrant to western
Alaska from Siberia.
Long-toed_Stint.Habitat:
Breeds in Siberian bogs and wet meadows. Winters
in Southeast Asia. Rare vagrant to western
Alaska.
Long-toed_Stint.Similar Looking Birds:
Least Sandpiper similar. Long-toed has longer toes,
yellow legs, and different head pattern.
Long-toed_Stint.Best Ways to Identify:
Long toes visible. Yellow legs. Bolder head pattern
with white supercilium. Rare vagrant
in western Alaska.

Louisiana_Waterthrush.Description: Warbler with white supercilium, brown back, streaked underparts, and buff wash on flanks. Bobs tail.
Louisiana_Waterthrush.Behavior: Walks along fast-moving streams bobbing tail continuously. Loud ringing song.
Louisiana_Waterthrush.Habitat: Fast-flowing forested streams in eastern North America.
Louisiana_Waterthrush.Similar Looking Birds: Northern Waterthrush prefers still water and has yellowish supercilium; Louisiana has white.
Louisiana_Waterthrush.Best Ways to Identify: Pure white supercilium, buffy flanks, and bobbing tail along fast-moving streams.

Lucifer_Hummingbird.Description:
Small hummingbird. Male has elongated iridescent
purple gorget that flares to sides. Long curved
bill. Female streaked below. About 3.5 inches.
Lucifer_Hummingbird.Behavior:
Feeds on agave and desert flowers. Males display
with pendulum swings. Found in desert canyons
and scrub of Big Bend area, Texas.
Lucifer_Hummingbird.Habitat:
Desert scrub with agave, rocky canyon slopes in
Big Bend area of Texas, and adjacent
Mexico.
Lucifer_Hummingbird.Similar Looking Birds:
Costa's Hummingbird similar purple gorget. Lucifer's
curved bill and elongated gorget extensions distinctive.
Lucifer_Hummingbird.Best Ways to Identify:
Male's dramatically elongated purple gorget extending
on sides. Long curved bill. Female's long
curved bill distinctive.

Lucys_Warbler.Description: Tiny plain gray warbler with white eye ring, chestnut rump patch, and chestnut crown patch.
Lucys_Warbler.Behavior: Only warbler that regularly nests in cavities, using abandoned woodpecker holes.
Lucys_Warbler.Habitat: Desert riparian areas with mesquite trees in the southwestern United States.
Lucys_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: Virginia's Warbler has yellow on breast; Lucy's is plain gray with chestnut rump.
Lucys_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: Tiny plain gray warbler with chestnut rump and crown -- nests in tree cavities.

MacGillivrays_Warbler.Description: Male has olive back, yellow underparts, gray hood with broken white eye crescents, and black bib.
MacGillivrays_Warbler.Behavior: Skulks in dense low vegetation, hard to see. Loud rolling song.
MacGillivrays_Warbler.Habitat: Dense brushy areas and riparian thickets in western North America.
MacGillivrays_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: Mourning Warbler is nearly identical but has complete hood; MacGillivray's has eye crescents.
MacGillivrays_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: Broken white eye crescents separate it from Mourning Warbler.

Magnificent_Frigatebird.Description:
Large black seabird with enormously long forked tail.
Male has brilliant red inflatable throat
pouch. About 40 inches.
Magnificent_Frigatebird.Behavior:
Kleptoparasite; chases other seabirds and steals food.
Soars effortlessly on thermals.
Breeds on Florida Keys and Caribbean.
Magnificent_Frigatebird.Habitat:
Tropical Atlantic and Pacific coasts. Regular along
Florida and Gulf coasts; breeds on
Dry Tortugas.
Magnificent_Frigatebird.Similar Looking Birds:
Great Frigatebird similar but found in Pacific/Indian
Ocean. Magnificent is Atlantic species.
Magnificent_Frigatebird.Best Ways to Identify:
Enormous long forked tail, all-black plumage. Male's
red throat pouch inflated at colony.
Common along Gulf and Florida coasts.

Magnolia_Warbler.Description: Male has black back, yellow underparts with black streaks, white wing patch, and yellow rump.
Magnolia_Warbler.Behavior: Active forager at mid-level in conifers. Bold white tail band visible from below.
Magnolia_Warbler.Habitat: Young coniferous and mixed forests; breeds in boreal forest.
Magnolia_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: Prairie Warbler has facial streaking; Magnolia has white wing patch and streaked yellow breast.
Magnolia_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: White wing patch, yellow rump, and yellow breast with black streaking.

Mallard.Description: Most familiar duck. Male has iridescent green head, yellow bill, white neck ring, and chestnut breast.
Mallard.Behavior: Dabbles for seeds and aquatic vegetation. Ancestor of most domestic duck breeds.
Mallard.Habitat: Almost any freshwater habitat across North America.
Mallard.Similar Looking Birds: Green head and yellow bill of male are distinctive; female resembles other female dabbling ducks.
Mallard.Best Ways to Identify: Male's iridescent green head and yellow bill -- the most recognized duck in the world.

Mandarin_Duck.Description:
Medium duck. Male extraordinarily colorful with orange
sail feathers, purple breast,
green crown, red bill. About 18 inches.
Mandarin_Duck.Behavior:
Perches in trees, nests in tree cavities. Small
introduced populations exist in
California and other areas.
Mandarin_Duck.Habitat:
Woodland near ponds and rivers. Escaped individuals
and small introduced populations
in North America.
Mandarin_Duck.Similar Looking Birds:
Wood Duck male similar flamboyance but different pattern.
No other duck looks
like breeding male Mandarin.
Mandarin_Duck.Best Ways to Identify:
Male unmistakable with orange sail feathers and
multicolored head. Most ornate duck
in world.

Mangrove_Cuckoo.Description: Slim cuckoo with gray-brown upperparts, buffy-yellow underparts, black mask, and long white-tipped tail.
Mangrove_Cuckoo.Behavior: Secretive and hard to see. Slow deliberate movements in dense mangrove vegetation.
Mangrove_Cuckoo.Habitat: Mangrove swamps and tropical hammocks of southern Florida.
Mangrove_Cuckoo.Similar Looking Birds: Yellow-billed Cuckoo lacks black mask and buffy underparts; Mangrove is distinctive.
Mangrove_Cuckoo.Best Ways to Identify: Black mask, buffy-yellow underparts, and mangrove habitat in southern Florida.

Mangrove_Swallow.Description:
Small swallow, iridescent green above with white
rump, white below. White loral
spot. About 5 inches.
Mangrove_Swallow.Behavior:
Forages over water near mangroves and rivers.
Nests in tree cavities. Rare
vagrant to southern Texas and Florida.
Mangrove_Swallow.Habitat:
Mangroves and coastal rivers from Mexico to Panama.
Very rare vagrant to southern
Texas and Florida.
Mangrove_Swallow.Similar Looking Birds:
Tree Swallow lacks white rump. Violet-green Swallow
has white patches on face
and white rump in different range.
Mangrove_Swallow.Best Ways to Identify:
White rump distinctive. Iridescent green above,
white below. White loral spot.
Coastal Mexico/Central America.

Mangrove_Yellow_(Yellow)_Warbler.Description:
Small warbler, bright yellow with chestnut head on
male in Caribbean subspecies.
About 5 inches.
Mangrove_Yellow_(Yellow)_Warbler.Behavior:
Forages in mangroves for insects. Resident in mangrove
forests of Caribbean and
Gulf Coast.
Mangrove_Yellow_(Yellow)_Warbler.Habitat:
Mangrove forests of Florida Keys, Gulf Coast, and
Caribbean. Non-migratory resident
subspecies group.
Mangrove_Yellow_(Yellow)_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds:
Northern Yellow Warbler lacks chestnut head. Wilson's
Warbler has black cap.
Chestnut head on male distinctive.
Mangrove_Yellow_(Yellow)_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify:
Male with chestnut head in Caribbean form. Mangrove
habitat. Yellow overall.
Resident non-migratory subspecies.

Manx_Shearwater.Description:
Medium shearwater, jet black above, bright white below,
sharp contrasting pattern, black bill.
About 13 inches.
Manx_Shearwater.Behavior:
Breeds on British and Irish islands. Common in North
Atlantic; migrates to South America.
Regular offshore Atlantic coast.
Manx_Shearwater.Habitat:
North Atlantic Ocean. Regular offshore Atlantic coast
in summer. Breeds in European
islands, winters off South America.
Manx_Shearwater.Similar Looking Birds:
Audubon's Shearwater similar but smaller with brown
(not black) back. Manx has sharp
black-and-white contrast.
Manx_Shearwater.Best Ways to Identify:
Sharp black-and-white contrast with jet-black upperparts.
Medium shearwater. Common
Atlantic coast seabird.

Marbled_Godwit.Description: Large shorebird with long upturned bill, cinnamon-brown plumage, and barred underparts.
Marbled_Godwit.Behavior: Probes deeply in mud for invertebrates. Flies long distances in V-shaped flocks.
Marbled_Godwit.Habitat: Coastal mudflats in winter; northern Great Plains grasslands for breeding.
Marbled_Godwit.Similar Looking Birds: Long-billed Curlew has downcurved bill; Godwit's bill is straight with slight upward bend.
Marbled_Godwit.Best Ways to Identify: Large cinnamon-brown shorebird with long pinkish-based slightly uptilted bill.

Marbled_Murrelet.Description: Seabird in breeding has marbled brown plumage; in winter has black-and-white with dark cap.
Marbled_Murrelet.Behavior: Uniquely nests on bare branches of old-growth trees far inland, not in burrows.
Marbled_Murrelet.Habitat: Old-growth coastal forests near the Pacific; forages at sea.
Marbled_Murrelet.Similar Looking Birds: Other murrelets nest underground; Marbled Murrelet nests in old-growth trees.
Marbled_Murrelet.Best Ways to Identify: Uses old-growth tree branches for nesting -- unusual for a seabird. Marbled brown in summer.

Mariana_Swiftlet.Description:
Small swift. Dark sooty gray-brown overall with paler
gray rump. Small size and forked tail.
About 4 inches.
Mariana_Swiftlet.Behavior:
Uses echolocation to navigate in dark caves where
it nests. Aerial insect feeder. Endangered; found
only in Mariana Islands and Guam.
Mariana_Swiftlet.Habitat:
Found only on Guam and northern Mariana Islands
(Saipan, Tinian, Aguijan). Nests in limestone
caves. Endangered species.
Mariana_Swiftlet.Similar Looking Birds:
Other small swiftlets. Mariana is only swiftlet
in its range.
Mariana_Swiftlet.Best Ways to Identify:
Only swiftlet in the Mariana Islands region. Small
size, dark plumage, and gray rump.
Nests in limestone caves.

Marsh_Sandpiper.Description:
Small elegant sandpiper. Gray-brown above, white
below, very thin straight bill, long pale legs.
Like a miniature Greenshank. About 9 inches.
Marsh_Sandpiper.Behavior:
Forages in shallow freshwater with delicate picking
movements. Rare vagrant to Pacific coast from
Eurasia.
Marsh_Sandpiper.Habitat:
Breeds in Eurasian steppe wetlands. Winters in
Africa and Asia. Rare vagrant to Pacific
coast of North America.
Marsh_Sandpiper.Similar Looking Birds:
Common Greenshank much larger. Wilson's Phalarope has
needle-thin bill.
Marsh_Sandpiper.Best Ways to Identify:
Very thin straight bill. Long pale legs. Delicate
Greenshank-like appearance. White rump
in flight.

Marsh_Wren.Description: Small wren with bold white supercilium, black-and-white streaked crown, and unstreaked rufous back.
Marsh_Wren.Behavior: Sings day and night from cattail marshes. Males build many dummy nests.
Marsh_Wren.Habitat: Dense cattail and bulrush marshes across North America.
Marsh_Wren.Similar Looking Birds: Sedge Wren has streaked crown and back; Marsh Wren has plain rufous back.
Marsh_Wren.Best Ways to Identify: Bold white eyebrow, streaked crown, and unstreaked rufous back in cattail marshes.

Masked_Booby.Description:
Large booby. White body and head with black flight
feathers and tail, yellow bill,
black face mask. About 32 inches.
Masked_Booby.Behavior:
Plunge-dives from height for fish. Breeds on tropical
islands; forages offshore in Atlantic
and Pacific.
Masked_Booby.Habitat:
Tropical oceans. Breeds on Dry Tortugas, Florida and
other Gulf/Caribbean islands. Offshore
Atlantic and Gulf.
Masked_Booby.Similar Looking Birds:
Nazca Booby nearly identical. Masked has yellow bill;
Nazca has orange bill.
Masked_Booby.Best Ways to Identify:
White plumage with black flight feathers, black mask.
Yellow bill; compare to Nazca Booby's
orange bill.

Masked_Duck.Description:
Small stiff-tailed duck. Male has rufous body and
bold black mask with blue bill. Female and non-breeding
male streaked brown with two facial stripes. About 13 inches.
Masked_Duck.Behavior:
Dives in dense aquatic vegetation. Secretive and
hard to spot. Rare visitor to Texas and Florida
from Mexico and Caribbean.
Masked_Duck.Similar Looking Birds:
Ruddy Duck same family. Female could be confused
with female Ruddy but facial stripe
pattern differs.
Masked_Duck.Best Ways to Identify:
Male's black face mask and reddish body with white
wing patch in flight. Female's two dark
facial stripes on pale face.

Masked_Tityra.Description:
Stocky bird, male pale gray with black mask, wings,
and tail tip, red bare facial skin.
Female brown and gray. About 8 inches.
Masked_Tityra.Behavior:
Eats fruit and some insects. Perches conspicuously at
forest canopy. Very rare vagrant
to southern Texas.
Masked_Tityra.Habitat:
Forest edge and open woodland from Mexico to South
America. Very rare vagrant to
southern Texas.
Masked_Tityra.Similar Looking Birds:
Black-and-white plumage pattern unique among cotingas.
Red facial skin distinctive.
Masked_Tityra.Best Ways to Identify:
Male: gray with black mask and red bare facial skin.
Cotinga family. Very rare
Texas vagrant from Mexico.

Maui-nui_Akialoa.Description:
Small Hawaiian honeycreeper, long decurved bill,
yellow-olive body. Extinct from
Lanai and Maui.
Maui-nui_Akialoa.Behavior:
Probed bark and flowers with long bill. Extinct
since approximately early 20th century.
Maui-nui_Akialoa.Habitat:
Native forests of Lanai and possibly Maui. Extinct
due to deforestation.
Maui-nui_Akialoa.Similar Looking Birds:
Other akialoa species island-specific, all extinct.
No similar birds survive in
Maui-nui island group.
Maui-nui_Akialoa.Best Ways to Identify:
Extinct. Long decurved bill, yellow-olive. Lanai and
Maui group. No longer exists.

Maui_Akepa.Description:
Small Hawaiian honeycreeper, male orange-yellow with
slightly crossed bill. Female
olive-green. Extinct early 1900s.
Maui_Akepa.Behavior:
Used crossed bill to open flower buds. Extinct from
Maui in early twentieth
century.
Maui_Akepa.Habitat: Native forests of Maui. Extinct due to deforestation.
Maui_Akepa.Similar Looking Birds:
Hawaii Akepa on Big Island. Akekee on Kauai. No
similar birds survive on Maui.
Maui_Akepa.Best Ways to Identify:
Extinct. Orange-yellow male, crossed bill. Maui.
No longer exists.

Maui_Alauahio.Description:
Small Hawaiian creeper. Male yellowish-green with
olive back. Female olive-green.
About 4.5 inches.
Maui_Alauahio.Behavior:
Actively creeps along branches and bark searching
for insects. Still present in
native forests of Maui.
Maui_Alauahio.Habitat:
Native ohia and koa forests of east Maui above
4,000 feet. Uncommon but persistent.
Maui_Alauahio.Similar Looking Birds:
Maui Amakihi has curved bill. Maui Warbler larger
with different behavior.
Only creeper remaining on Maui.
Maui_Alauahio.Best Ways to Identify:
Small yellowish-green bird creeping along branches
on Maui. Active bark searcher.
Native forest above 4,000 feet.

Maui_Nukupuu.Description:
Small Hawaiian honeycreeper, long strongly decurved
bill, yellow male with greenish
back. About 5.5 inches.
Maui_Nukupuu.Behavior:
Used long bill to probe bark for insects. Possibly
extinct; last confirmed record
in the 1990s on Maui.
Maui_Nukupuu.Habitat:
Native wet forests of east Maui. Possibly extinct
due to avian malaria and
habitat degradation.
Maui_Nukupuu.Similar Looking Birds:
Maui Alauahio has short bill. Iiwi much larger
and red. Long bill distinctive.
Maui_Nukupuu.Best Ways to Identify:
Very long strongly decurved bill, yellow male. East
Maui wet forest. Possibly
extinct. Last records 1990s.

Maui_Parrotbill.Description:
Small Hawaiian honeycreeper, olive-green above, yellow
below, massive hooked parrot-like
bill. About 5.5 inches.
Maui_Parrotbill.Behavior:
Uses massive bill to tear bark and branches for
insects. Critically endangered; fewer
than 500 individuals remain.
Maui_Parrotbill.Habitat:
Native wet forest of east Maui above 4,500 feet.
Very restricted range.
Maui_Parrotbill.Similar Looking Birds:
Maui Alauahio creeps on bark but smaller bill.
Ou has yellow head.
No other hookbill on Maui.
Maui_Parrotbill.Best Ways to Identify:
Massive hooked bill, olive-green above, yellow below.
High Maui native forest.
Critically endangered endemic.

McCowns_Longspur.Description: Stocky sparrow-like bird; breeding male has black cap, breast patch, and gray back; white tail with black T-shape.
McCowns_Longspur.Behavior: Forages on ground for seeds and insects; male sings in flight display; flocks in winter on bare fields.
McCowns_Longspur.Habitat: Short-grass prairies, plowed fields, and sparse rangeland of Great Plains; winters in Texas and Mexico.
McCowns_Longspur.Similar Looking Birds: Chestnut-collared Longspur has chestnut nape; Thick-billed Longspur has heavier bill and different tail pattern.
McCowns_Longspur.Best Ways to Identify: White tail with inverted T-shaped black tip; heavy bill; breeding male's black chest patch; short primary projection.

McKays_Bunting.Description:
Medium bunting, almost entirely white with small
black wing tips. Female with
some brown. About 6.5 inches.
McKays_Bunting.Behavior:
Forages on ground for seeds and insects. Breeds
only on St. Matthew and Hall
Islands, Alaska.
McKays_Bunting.Habitat:
Tundra of St. Matthew and Hall Islands in Bering
Sea. Winters on mainland
Alaska and occasionally coast.
McKays_Bunting.Similar Looking Birds:
Snow Bunting has more extensive black in wings
and back. Nearly all-white
pattern distinctive.
McKays_Bunting.Best Ways to Identify:
Almost entirely white with minimal black wing tips.
St. Matthew Island breeder.
More white than Snow Bunting.

Medium_Egret.Description:
Medium-sized white egret, yellow bill, black legs
and feet. Similar to Great Egret but
smaller. About 26 inches.
Medium_Egret.Behavior:
Wades in shallow water for fish. Asian and African
species; very rare vagrant to
western Alaska.
Medium_Egret.Habitat:
Wetlands and rice paddies of Asia and Africa. Very
rare vagrant to western Alaska
from East Asia.
Medium_Egret.Similar Looking Birds:
Great Egret larger with longer neck. Snowy Egret
has yellow feet. Medium Egret intermediate.
Medium_Egret.Best Ways to Identify:
All-white egret with yellow bill and black legs and
feet. Smaller than Great Egret.
Rare Alaska vagrant.

Merlin.Description: Small aggressive falcon with blue-gray or brown upperparts, heavily streaked underparts, and banded tail.
Merlin.Behavior: Pursues songbirds in fast dashing flight. Bold and aggressive for its small size.
Merlin.Habitat: Open country, forest edges, and cities across North America.
Merlin.Similar Looking Birds: American Kestrel has rusty back; Merlin is darker and lacks kestrel's black facial marks.
Merlin.Best Ways to Identify: Small compact falcon, heavily streaked below, dashing fast flight after small birds.

Mexican_Chickadee.Description:
Medium chickadee, black cap and bib, gray back
and wings, gray sides extending
far onto flanks. About 5 inches.
Mexican_Chickadee.Behavior:
Forages actively for insects and seeds in pine
and pine-oak forests. Less gregarious
than other chickadees.
Mexican_Chickadee.Habitat:
Pine and pine-oak forests of the Sierra Madre
Occidental, with small U.S. population
in Chiricahua Mountains, Arizona.
Mexican_Chickadee.Similar Looking Birds:
Mountain Chickadee has white supercilium. Black-capped
Chickadee has white cheeks
and buff sides.
Mexican_Chickadee.Best Ways to Identify:
Extensive dark gray wash on flanks and sides.
Black cap and bib. Chiricahua
Mountains, Arizona or Mexico.

Mexican_Duck.Description:
Large dabbling duck, closely related to Mallard.
Both sexes mottled brown similar to female Mallard.
Males have yellow-green bill. About 22 inches.
Mexican_Duck.Habitat:
Desert rivers, ponds, and wetlands in New Mexico,
Texas, and Mexico. Prefers rivers with
cottonwood and willow vegetation.
Mexican_Duck.Similar Looking Birds:
Female Mallard nearly identical. Hybridization
makes identification of pure individuals difficult.
Mexican_Duck.Best Ways to Identify:
Mottled brown plumage throughout. Male has yellower
bill than female Mallard. Best identified
by range and darker overall tone.

Mexican_Jay.Description:
Medium jay, blue-gray above, gray below, no streaking
on throat. No crest. Blue wings
and tail. About 11 inches.
Mexican_Jay.Behavior:
Highly social, lives in permanent flocks of related
birds. Cooperative breeding common.
Loud and conspicuous.
Mexican_Jay.Habitat:
Oak and pine-oak woodlands of the Madrean sky
islands in Arizona, New Mexico,
and Texas into Mexico.
Mexican_Jay.Similar Looking Birds:
Woodhouse's Scrub-Jay has white throat streaking.
Steller's Jay has crest and
is darker.
Mexican_Jay.Best Ways to Identify:
Plain gray-blue jay with no white throat streaks
and no crest. Sky island
oak woodland specialist.

Mexican_Violetear.Description:
Medium hummingbird. Brilliant metallic green body,
iridescent blue-violet ear patch on sides of
head. Blue-green tail band. About 4.5 inches.
Mexican_Violetear.Behavior:
Males sing persistently from prominent perches. Feeds
on nectar and small insects. Rare vagrant to
Texas and southern US from Mexico.
Mexican_Violetear.Habitat:
Mountain forests of Mexico and Central America.
Rare visitor to southern Texas; occasionally wanders
north to other US states.
Mexican_Violetear.Similar Looking Birds:
Broad-billed Hummingbird. Mexican Violetear's violet
ear patches diagnostic.
Mexican_Violetear.Best Ways to Identify:
Metallic green plumage with distinctive blue-violet
ear patches on sides of face.
Persistent singing from treetops.

Mexican_Whip-poor-will.Description:
Medium nightjar with cryptic brown, black, and gray
patterned plumage. Recently split from Eastern
Whip-poor-will. About 10 inches.
Mexican_Whip-poor-will.Behavior:
Nocturnal; catches flying insects at night. Roosts
on forest floor by day. Found in mountain
forests of southwest US and Mexico.
Mexican_Whip-poor-will.Habitat:
Pine-oak and mixed mountain forests of Arizona, New
Mexico, and west Texas. Winters in
Mexico and Central America.
Mexican_Whip-poor-will.Similar Looking Birds:
Eastern Whip-poor-will nearly identical; recently split.
Separated by range in western mountains.
Mexican_Whip-poor-will.Best Ways to Identify:
Nearly identical to Eastern Whip-poor-will. Range in
southwestern mountain forests key. Call
slightly different from eastern counterpart.

Middendorffs_Grasshopper_Warbler.Description:
Medium grasshopper warbler, brown above with streaked
crown, whitish below, pale supercilium.
Rounded tail. About 6 inches.
Middendorffs_Grasshopper_Warbler.Behavior:
Skulks in dense grass and scrub. Rare vagrant
to western Alaska and Aleutian
Islands.
Middendorffs_Grasshopper_Warbler.Habitat:
Dense grass, scrub, and sedge meadows in northeastern
Asia. Rare vagrant to western
Alaska.
Middendorffs_Grasshopper_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds:
Lanceolated Warbler smaller and more heavily streaked.
Pallas's Grasshopper Warbler has
spotted breast.
Middendorffs_Grasshopper_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify:
Larger grasshopper warbler with plain white underparts.
Western Alaska vagrant. Skulking
in dense grass or scrub.

Millerbird.Description:
Small reed warbler endemic to Northwestern Hawaiian
Islands. Brown above, buff-white
below. About 5 inches.
Millerbird.Behavior:
Skulking and hard to see. Moves through dense
vegetation searching for insects.
Species was relocated to save it.
Millerbird.Habitat:
Dense low vegetation on Nihoa and now Laysan
Islands in the Northwestern Hawaiian
Islands.
Millerbird.Similar Looking Birds:
No similar species in its isolated island habitat.
Unique Hawaiian endemic
reed warbler.
Millerbird.Best Ways to Identify:
Location is definitive: Northwestern Hawaiian Islands.
Small brown warbler, skulking
behavior. No look-alikes present.

Mississippi_Kite.Description: Elegant gray raptor with pale head, dark wings, red eyes, and square black tail.
Mississippi_Kite.Behavior: Catches and eats large insects in flight. Often soars in groups on thermals.
Mississippi_Kite.Habitat: Open woodlands, riparian areas, and towns in the south-central United States.
Mississippi_Kite.Similar Looking Birds: White-tailed Kite has white body and tail; Mississippi Kite is uniformly gray.
Mississippi_Kite.Best Ways to Identify: Pale gray head, dark gray body, red eye, and square black tail -- graceful insect-eating hawk.

Mistle_Thrush.Description:
Large thrush, gray-brown above with heavily spotted
white underparts, white underwings.
About 11 inches.
Mistle_Thrush.Behavior:
Bold and fearless, known as stormcock for singing
in harsh weather. Very rare
vagrant to North America.
Mistle_Thrush.Habitat:
Open woodland, parks, and farmland in Europe and
Asia. Very rare vagrant to
North America.
Mistle_Thrush.Similar Looking Birds:
Song Thrush smaller with buffy wash below. American
Robin has orange-red
breast, not spotted.
Mistle_Thrush.Best Ways to Identify:
Large size, heavily spotted white underparts, gray-brown
above. White underwings.
Very rare European vagrant.

Mitred_Parakeet.Description:
Large green parakeet with variable red patches on
face and head. Long pointed tail,
orange bill. About 15 inches.
Mitred_Parakeet.Behavior:
Established feral population in Los Angeles area.
Loud flocking behavior. Mixes with
other feral parakeets.
Mitred_Parakeet.Habitat:
Established in suburban Southern California, particularly
Los Angeles area.
Mitred_Parakeet.Similar Looking Birds:
Red-masked Parakeet has more extensive red on head.
Mitred has variable scattered red.
Mitred_Parakeet.Best Ways to Identify:
Large green parakeet with variable red scattered on
head and face. Los Angeles area
feral population.

Monk_Parakeet.Description:
Medium green parrot with gray breast and face, long
pointed tail. Builds large stick nests.
About 11 inches.
Monk_Parakeet.Habitat:
Established in cities and suburbs in Florida, Texas,
Illinois, and other states. Lives
year-round outdoors.
Monk_Parakeet.Similar Looking Birds:
Other green parakeets lack gray breast. Monk Parakeet's
gray face and breast distinctive.
Monk_Parakeet.Best Ways to Identify:
Green with gray breast and face. Builds large communal
stick nests on power poles.
Found in many US cities.

Montezuma_Quail.Description:
Chunky round quail. Male has bold black and white
face pattern, chestnut sides with white spots, blue-gray
breast. Female cryptically brown-streaked. About 9 inches.
Montezuma_Quail.Behavior:
Probes soil with strong claws for bulbs and tubers.
Freezes when disturbed rather than flushing.
Found in montane pine-oak woodlands.
Montezuma_Quail.Habitat:
Rocky pine-oak and oak woodlands in mountain
grasslands of southeastern Arizona, New Mexico,
and Texas into Mexico.
Montezuma_Quail.Similar Looking Birds:
Other quail species in range. Male's harlequin
face pattern unmistakable; female more difficult.
Montezuma_Quail.Best Ways to Identify:
Male's harlequin black and white face pattern unique.
Round body shape and spotted sides distinctive
even in female.

Morelets_Seedeater.Description:
Tiny finch. Male black above with white collar, white
below. Female plain brown.
About 4.5 inches.
Morelets_Seedeater.Behavior:
Forages for grass seeds in tall grass. Small population
resident in Rio Grande Valley,
Texas.
Morelets_Seedeater.Habitat:
Tall native grasses along the Rio Grande and adjacent
areas in south Texas.
Morelets_Seedeater.Similar Looking Birds:
White-collared Seedeater very similar. Black-and-white
pattern on tiny finch
distinctive.
Morelets_Seedeater.Best Ways to Identify:
Male tiny black-and-white with white collar. Tall
grass along Rio Grande, Texas.
Resident in specific grass areas.

Mottled_Duck.Description: Medium-sized dabbling duck with mottled brown plumage; buffy face and throat; blue-purple speculum with black borders.
Mottled_Duck.Behavior: Resident non-migratory duck; pairs year-round; dabbles in shallow water for aquatic vegetation and invertebrates.
Mottled_Duck.Habitat: Coastal marshes, estuaries, and freshwater wetlands along Gulf Coast from Florida to Texas.
Mottled_Duck.Similar Looking Birds: Female Mallard has orange-sided bill and white tail; American Black Duck has darker body and different speculum.
Mottled_Duck.Best Ways to Identify: Clean buffy unmarked throat and face; blue speculum with narrow black borders; no white in tail; Gulf Coast.

Mottled_Owl.Description:
Medium owl, brown mottled plumage, round head without
ear tufts, dark eyes.
About 14 inches.
Mottled_Owl.Behavior:
Nocturnal forest hunter. Rare vagrant to southern
Texas from Mexico. Calls with
hooting series.
Mottled_Owl.Habitat:
Tropical forest of Mexico and Central America. Rare
vagrant to southern Texas.
Mottled_Owl.Similar Looking Birds:
Barred Owl similar but larger. Mottled Owl more
uniformly brown and mottled.
Mottled_Owl.Best Ways to Identify:
Medium round-headed owl, mottled brown, dark eyes.
Very rare Texas vagrant from
Mexican tropical forest.

Mottled_Petrel.Description:
Medium gadfly petrel with distinctive dark gray belly
patch, white face and underparts,
dark diagonal bar on underwing. About 14 inches.
Mottled_Petrel.Behavior:
Breeds on New Zealand islands; migrates into North
Pacific in winter. Occasional off Pacific
coast.
Mottled_Petrel.Habitat:
North Pacific Ocean in winter. Occasional visitor
to Pacific coast; breeds on New
Zealand islands.
Mottled_Petrel.Similar Looking Birds:
Other gadfly petrels lack dark belly patch. Mottled
Petrel's dark belly unique.
Mottled_Petrel.Best Ways to Identify:
Dark gray belly patch contrasting with white face
and throat. Dark diagonal bar on
underwing. North Pacific visitor.

Mountain_Bluebird.Description: Male is brilliant sky-blue overall -- no rusty color anywhere. Female is gray with blue tinges.
Mountain_Bluebird.Behavior: Hovers over meadows to spot insects on the ground. Nests in tree cavities and boxes.
Mountain_Bluebird.Habitat: Open mountain meadows, sagebrush, and grasslands of western North America.
Mountain_Bluebird.Similar Looking Birds: Eastern Bluebird has rusty breast; Western Bluebird has rusty back; Mountain is all blue.
Mountain_Bluebird.Best Ways to Identify: All sky-blue male with no rust -- hovers over open mountain meadows.

Mountain_Chickadee.Description: Chickadee with white supercilium stripe through black cap, gray back, and white cheeks.
Mountain_Chickadee.Behavior: Caches seeds for winter. Highly cold-tolerant resident of high-elevation forests.
Mountain_Chickadee.Habitat: Coniferous forests at middle and upper elevations in western mountains.
Mountain_Chickadee.Similar Looking Birds: Black-capped Chickadee lacks the white stripe through the black cap.
Mountain_Chickadee.Best Ways to Identify: White stripe through black cap is the key field mark distinguishing it from Black-capped.

Mountain_Plover.Description: Plain sandy-brown plover with no wing stripe, thin white supercilium, and black forecrown in breeding.
Mountain_Plover.Behavior: Runs on the ground in dry open areas rather than near water. Very hard to spot.
Mountain_Plover.Habitat: Dry shortgrass prairie and bare ground in the western Great Plains.
Mountain_Plover.Similar Looking Birds: Killdeer has two breast bands; other plovers have white breast band; Mountain Plover is plain.
Mountain_Plover.Best Ways to Identify: Plain tan plover with no breast bands -- drier habitat than all other North American plovers.

Mountain_Quail.Description: Plump quail with long straight head plume, chestnut throat, bold white barring on chestnut flanks.
Mountain_Quail.Behavior: Walks along mountain slopes foraging for seeds and bulbs. Hard to observe.
Mountain_Quail.Habitat: Dense chaparral and mountain brush of the Pacific Coast ranges.
Mountain_Quail.Similar Looking Birds: California Quail has teardrop-shaped plume and lacks chestnut flanks; Mountain is larger.
Mountain_Quail.Best Ways to Identify: Long straight head plume, chestnut throat, and bold white-barred flanks.

Mourning_Dove.Description: Slender dove with long pointed tail, pinkish body, black spots on wing, and iridescent neck.
Mourning_Dove.Behavior: One of the most abundant birds in North America. Mournful cooing call.
Mourning_Dove.Habitat: Open fields, roadsides, gardens, and woodlands across North America.
Mourning_Dove.Similar Looking Birds: White-winged Dove has white wing patch; Mourning Dove has long pointed tail.
Mourning_Dove.Best Ways to Identify: Long pointed tail and mournful cooing call -- most abundant game bird in North America.

Mourning_Warbler.Description: Male has olive back, yellow underparts, gray hood with complete black bib. Female has pale throat.
Mourning_Warbler.Behavior: Skulks in dense low shrubs. Song a rolling churry-churry-churry.
Mourning_Warbler.Habitat: Dense shrubby habitats and forest edges in northern and eastern North America.
Mourning_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: MacGillivray's Warbler has broken white eye crescents; Mourning has complete hood.
Mourning_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: Complete gray hood without eye crescents -- western counterpart is MacGillivray's Warbler.

Mugimaki_Flycatcher.Description:
Small flycatcher. Male black above with orange breast
and white wing patch. Female
brown. About 5 inches.
Mugimaki_Flycatcher.Behavior:
Sallies from perch for flying insects in forest.
Very rare vagrant to western
Alaska from East Asia.
Mugimaki_Flycatcher.Habitat:
Coniferous and mixed forest of East Asia and Siberia.
Very rare vagrant to western
Alaska.
Mugimaki_Flycatcher.Similar Looking Birds:
Narcissus Flycatcher more yellow. American Redstart
has white belly. Different
pattern from other Ficedula.
Mugimaki_Flycatcher.Best Ways to Identify:
Male black above with orange breast and white wing
patch. Very rare Alaska
vagrant from Siberia/Japan.

Murphys_Petrel.Description:
Medium dark gadfly petrel, gray-brown overall, pale
primary bases forming white flash,
pale gray face. About 15 inches.
Murphys_Petrel.Behavior:
Breeds on central South Pacific islands. Migrates
north into North Pacific; regular
rare visitor off California.
Murphys_Petrel.Habitat:
North Pacific in non-breeding season. Regular but
rare offshore California in
spring migration.
Murphys_Petrel.Similar Looking Birds:
Providence Petrel larger and darker. Cook's Petrel
smaller and paler.
Murphys_Petrel.Best Ways to Identify:
Medium gray-brown gadfly petrel in North Pacific.
Pale face, white primary flash
from below. Spring migrant off California.

Muscovy_Duck.Description: A large, heavy duck with dark iridescent plumage and distinctive red facial caruncles (fleshy knobs). Males much larger than females.
Muscovy_Duck.Behavior: Forages for plants, seeds, fish, and insects. Perches readily in trees. Largely silent compared to other ducks; males produce a low hiss.
Muscovy_Duck.Habitat: Tropical forests near rivers and lakes in Central and South America. Widely domesticated; feral populations established worldwide.
Muscovy_Duck.Similar Looking Birds: Domestic Muscovy ducks vary widely in color. Wild birds could be confused with large dark ducks but red facial caruncles are unique.
Muscovy_Duck.Best Ways to Identify: Prominent red or red-and-black fleshy caruncles around the face and bill base are diagnostic. Large size and dark iridescent plumage confirm identity.

Mute_Swan.Description: Introduced very large white swan with orange bill, black knob at base, and graceful S-curved neck.
Mute_Swan.Behavior: Holds wings arched over back in defensive posture. Less vocal than native swans.
Mute_Swan.Habitat: Lakes, ponds, and coastal bays; introduced from Europe to eastern North America.
Mute_Swan.Similar Looking Birds: Tundra Swan has yellow spot at bill base and black bill; Mute Swan has orange bill with black knob.
Mute_Swan.Best Ways to Identify: Orange bill with black knob and habit of arching wings over back when threatened.

Nanday_Parakeet.Description:
Medium green parrot with black head, blue breast band,
red thighs, long pointed tail.
About 13 inches.
Nanday_Parakeet.Behavior:
Established feral populations in Florida and California.
Loud and conspicuous; roosts
communally.
Nanday_Parakeet.Habitat:
Established in Florida (St. Petersburg area) and Southern
California in suburban and urban
habitats.
Nanday_Parakeet.Similar Looking Birds:
Other green parakeets lack black head. Nanday's black
head distinctive.
Nanday_Parakeet.Best Ways to Identify:
Green with black head. Blue breast wash, red thighs.
Long tail. Feral populations in
Florida and Southern California.

Narcissus_Flycatcher.Description:
Small flycatcher. Male brilliant orange-yellow below
with black above and white wing
patch. Female brown. About 5 inches.
Narcissus_Flycatcher.Behavior:
Sallies from perch for insects. Rare vagrant to
western Alaska and Aleutian Islands
from East Asia.
Narcissus_Flycatcher.Habitat:
Mixed and deciduous forest of Japan and East Asia.
Rare vagrant to western Alaska.
Narcissus_Flycatcher.Similar Looking Birds:
American Redstart has different pattern. No other
bright orange-yellow small flycatcher
in Alaska.
Narcissus_Flycatcher.Best Ways to Identify:
Male brilliant orange-yellow with black above, white
wing patch. Rare Alaska vagrant
from Japan.

Nashville_Warbler.Description: Compact warbler with gray head, white eye ring, yellow underparts, olive back, and hidden rusty crown.
Nashville_Warbler.Behavior: Actively gleans insects from shrubs and trees at low to mid levels.
Nashville_Warbler.Habitat: Breeds in brushy openings and bogs in northeastern and western forests.
Nashville_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: Connecticut Warbler has complete eye ring and larger size; Nashville has plain gray head.
Nashville_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: Gray head, complete white eye ring, and yellow underparts with no streaking.

Naumanns_Thrush.Description:
Medium thrush, brown above with rufous-orange tail
and underparts patterning, white
supercilium. About 9 inches.
Naumanns_Thrush.Behavior:
Forages on ground for berries and invertebrates.
Very rare vagrant to Alaska
and western North America from Asia.
Naumanns_Thrush.Habitat:
Open woodland, scrub, and farmland in Siberia and
East Asia. Very rare vagrant
to Alaska.
Naumanns_Thrush.Similar Looking Birds:
Dusky Thrush darker overall. Eyebrowed Thrush
lacks rufous tail. Fieldfare
has gray head.
Naumanns_Thrush.Best Ways to Identify:
Rufous-orange tail and chest patches on brown thrush.
Very rare Alaska and west
coast vagrant from Asia.

Nazca_Booby.Description:
Large booby, white body with black flight feathers
and tail, orange bill, black face mask.
About 32 inches.
Nazca_Booby.Behavior:
Replaced Masked Booby in Galapagos region. Plunge-dives
for fish. Rare vagrant to Pacific
coast of North America.
Nazca_Booby.Similar Looking Birds:
Masked Booby nearly identical but has yellow bill.
Nazca Booby's orange bill diagnostic.
Nazca_Booby.Best Ways to Identify:
White booby with black flight feathers. Orange bill
distinguishes from Masked Booby's
yellow bill. Rare Pacific vagrant.

Nelsons_Sparrow.Description: Small sparrow with orange-buff face and breast, gray nape and cheek, streaked gray and white sides.
Nelsons_Sparrow.Behavior: Skulks in salt marshes and wet grass. Very secretive and hard to flush.
Nelsons_Sparrow.Habitat: Coastal salt marshes and interior wet meadows in eastern North America.
Nelsons_Sparrow.Similar Looking Birds: LeConte's Sparrow is brighter orange; Saltmarsh Sparrow has more contrast; similar habitat.
Nelsons_Sparrow.Best Ways to Identify: Orange-buff face, gray cheeks, and blurry streaking on sides in salt marshes.

Neotropic_Cormorant.Description:
Small dark cormorant with long tail, small yellow
throat pouch bordered by white.
About 26 inches.
Neotropic_Cormorant.Behavior:
Dives for fish in freshwater and coastal areas. Common
in Texas and southwestern US; expanding
northward and eastward.
Neotropic_Cormorant.Habitat:
Inland fresh water, coastal marshes and ponds. Common
in Texas, Louisiana, and expanding
north and east.
Neotropic_Cormorant.Similar Looking Birds:
Double-crested Cormorant larger with orange throat.
Neotropic smaller with white-bordered
yellow throat pouch.
Neotropic_Cormorant.Best Ways to Identify:
Small size, long tail, white-bordered yellow throat
pouch. Common at Texas freshwater
ponds and coastal areas.

Newells_Shearwater.Description:
Medium shearwater, black above, white below, white
undertail coverts. Similar to Manx but
with white extending up sides. About 13 inches.
Newells_Shearwater.Behavior:
Breeds on Hawaiian mountains. Endangered; declining
from predators and light attraction.
Forages offshore Hawaiian waters.
Newells_Shearwater.Habitat:
Hawaiian offshore waters. Breeds on high volcanic
slopes of Hawaiian Islands.
Endangered species.
Newells_Shearwater.Similar Looking Birds:
Manx Shearwater nearly identical. Newell's has more
white on sides and undertail.
Newells_Shearwater.Best Ways to Identify:
Black above with white below extending more onto flanks.
Hawaiian species. Nearly identical
to Manx Shearwater.

Nihoa_Finch.Description:
Medium Hawaiian honeycreeper, yellow head and underparts,
streaked brown back, large
finch bill. About 6 inches.
Nihoa_Finch.Behavior:
Omnivorous forager, bold and active. Found only on
tiny Nihoa Island in
Northwestern Hawaiian Islands.
Nihoa_Finch.Habitat:
Nihoa Island in the Northwestern Hawaiian Islands.
Rocky slopes with low vegetation
and beach strand.
Nihoa_Finch.Similar Looking Birds:
Laysan Finch similar but on different island. No
other large finch on tiny
Nihoa Island.
Nihoa_Finch.Best Ways to Identify:
Yellow finch with large bill on Nihoa Island only.
No other similar bird
present. Bold and inquisitive.

Northern_Beardless-Tyrannulet.Description:
Tiny flycatcher, olive-gray above, whitish below with
two wing bars, small bill, slight
crest. About 4 inches.
Northern_Beardless-Tyrannulet.Behavior:
Gleans insects from foliage. Found in riparian and
dry scrub in southern Arizona
and Texas.
Northern_Beardless-Tyrannulet.Habitat:
Riparian thickets and dry thorn scrub in southern
Arizona and southern Texas.
Year-round resident.
Northern_Beardless-Tyrannulet.Similar Looking Birds:
Empidonax flycatchers similar but larger. Beardless-Tyrannulet
tiny with small bill.
Northern_Beardless-Tyrannulet.Best Ways to Identify:
Tiny olive-gray flycatcher with small bill. Two wing
bars. Whistle call. Southern
Arizona and Texas resident.

Northern_Bobwhite.Description: Small quail with bold black-and-white head pattern on male, mottled brown plumage, and short tail.
Northern_Bobwhite.Behavior: Lives in coveys that explode upward when flushed. Familiar bob-WHITE whistle call.
Northern_Bobwhite.Habitat: Brushy fields, grasslands, and open pine forests of eastern North America.
Northern_Bobwhite.Similar Looking Birds: California Quail has topknot; other quails lack the bob-white striped head pattern.
Northern_Bobwhite.Best Ways to Identify: Bold black-and-white facial stripes on male and whistled bob-WHITE call.

Northern_Boobook.Description:
Medium owl, brown with white-spotted plumage, round
head, large yellow eyes. No ear tufts.
About 11 inches.
Northern_Boobook.Behavior:
Migratory owl from East Asia. Rare vagrant to Aleutian
Islands and western Alaska.
Northern_Boobook.Habitat:
Forest and woodland of East Asia. Rare vagrant to
Aleutian Islands and western
Alaska.
Northern_Boobook.Similar Looking Birds:
Spotted Owl similar but much larger. Northern Boobook
smaller with round head.
Northern_Boobook.Best Ways to Identify:
Medium round-headed owl with yellow eyes. Brown with
white spots. Rare vagrant to
western Alaska from Asia.

Northern_Cardinal.Description: Male is entirely brilliant red with black mask and prominent crest. Female is brown with red tinges.
Northern_Cardinal.Behavior: Year-round resident at bird feeders. Male feeds female during courtship.
Northern_Cardinal.Habitat: Forest edges, gardens, and shrubby areas across eastern and central North America.
Northern_Cardinal.Similar Looking Birds: Pyrrhuloxia has gray body with red tinges and parrot-like bill in the desert southwest.
Northern_Cardinal.Best Ways to Identify: Male is entirely red with crest and black mask -- unmistakable and beloved backyard bird.

Northern_Flicker.Description: Large woodpecker with barred brown back, spotted underparts, and yellow or red under wings and tail.
Northern_Flicker.Behavior: Often forages on the ground for ants. Loud wicker-wicker-wicker call.
Northern_Flicker.Habitat: Open woodlands and forest edges across North America.
Northern_Flicker.Similar Looking Birds: Gilded Flicker is all yellow-shafted; Northern has yellow (east) or red (west) under wings.
Northern_Flicker.Best Ways to Identify: Brown with spotted underparts, red or yellow flash under wings in flight, ground-foraging.

Northern_Fulmar.Description:
Stocky seabird, gray and white (light morph) or all
dark (dark morph), thick yellow tube-nose
bill, stiff-winged gliding flight. About 19 inches.
Northern_Fulmar.Behavior:
Common North Atlantic and Pacific seabird. Stiff-winged
gliding flight over waves. Follows
fishing boats.
Northern_Fulmar.Habitat:
North Atlantic and Pacific Oceans. Breeds on Arctic
cliffs; winters offshore. Common
from Alaska to California.
Northern_Fulmar.Similar Looking Birds:
Gulls lack tube-nose and have more flexible wing
beats. Fulmars glide stiffly.
Northern_Fulmar.Best Ways to Identify:
Stiff-winged gliding flight on flat wings. Thick yellow
tube-nose bill. Gray and white
or all-dark plumage.

Northern_Gannet.Description:
Large seabird, brilliant white with golden-buff head,
black wingtips, blue-ringed eye, pointed
tail. About 37 inches.
Northern_Gannet.Behavior:
Spectacular plunge-diver; dives from height to catch
fish. Common in North Atlantic.
Breeds on rocky Atlantic islands.
Northern_Gannet.Habitat:
North Atlantic Ocean. Breeds on rocky islands; common
offshore Atlantic coast in winter
and migration.
Northern_Gannet.Similar Looking Birds:
No other large white seabird combines golden head
with black wingtips in North Atlantic.
Northern_Gannet.Best Ways to Identify:
Brilliant white with golden head and black wingtips.
Spectacular plunge-diving. Very
common North Atlantic seabird.

Northern_Giant-Petrel.Description:
Very large petrel. Dark brown overall, massive
pale pink bill with reddish-brown tip.
About 35 inches.
Northern_Giant-Petrel.Behavior:
Carrion scavenger and predator. Breeds on subantarctic
islands. Very rare vagrant to North
American Pacific coast.
Northern_Giant-Petrel.Habitat:
Southern Ocean. Very rare vagrant to North American
Pacific coast. Resembles a small
albatross in flight.
Northern_Giant-Petrel.Similar Looking Birds:
Southern Giant-Petrel very similar but bill tip color
differs. Both are very rare in North America.
Northern_Giant-Petrel.Best Ways to Identify:
Massive pale bill, huge dark petrel. Hunched posture.
Very rare southern vagrant.
Resembles small dark albatross.

Northern_Goshawk.Description: Large accipiter with blue-gray back, finely barred gray underparts, bold white supercilium, and red eye.
Northern_Goshawk.Behavior: Aggressive nester that attacks humans near its nest. Hunts birds and mammals in forest.
Northern_Goshawk.Habitat: Mature boreal and mountain coniferous forests across North America.
Northern_Goshawk.Similar Looking Birds: Cooper's Hawk is smaller; Sharp-shinned is much smaller; Goshawk is crow-sized.
Northern_Goshawk.Best Ways to Identify: Crow-sized accipiter with bold white supercilium, finely barred gray underparts, and red eye.

Northern_Harrier.Description: Slender hawk with long tail, white rump patch, flat facial disc, and low quartering flight.
Northern_Harrier.Behavior: Flies low over marshes and fields tilting side to side listening for prey.
Northern_Harrier.Habitat: Open marshes, fields, and prairie across North America.
Northern_Harrier.Similar Looking Birds: No other hawk has white rump patch combined with flat facial disc and low quartering flight.
Northern_Harrier.Best Ways to Identify: White rump patch and low quartering flight over open marshes -- facial disc unique among hawks.

Northern_Hawk_Owl.Description:
Medium owl with long tail, hawk-like posture. Brown
barred below, white-spotted above,
black facial border. About 15 inches.
Northern_Hawk_Owl.Behavior:
Diurnal hunter perching at treetops. Irruptive visitor
to northern US from boreal forest.
Conspicuous and unafraid of humans.
Northern_Hawk_Owl.Habitat:
Boreal forest. Irruptive visitor from Canada to northern
tier states and New England.
Perches prominently.
Northern_Hawk_Owl.Similar Looking Birds:
Other owls lack hawk-like long tail and diurnal habits.
Northern Hawk Owl's shape unmistakable.
Northern_Hawk_Owl.Best Ways to Identify:
Long tail, hawk-like shape. Perches conspicuously at
treetop. Diurnal. Boreal irruptive
visitor to northern US.

Northern_House_Wren.Description:
Small brown wren, plain brown above with barred
wings and tail, pale supercilium.
Very common. About 5 inches.
Northern_House_Wren.Behavior:
Energetic and vocal, sings a loud bubbling song.
Nests in cavities including nest
boxes. Cocks tail upward.
Northern_House_Wren.Habitat:
Forest edges, gardens, thickets, and suburbs across
North America. One of commonest
cavity-nesting birds.
Northern_House_Wren.Similar Looking Birds:
Winter Wren smaller, darker, shorter tail. Pacific
Wren similar to Winter.
Bewick's Wren has long flat tail.
Northern_House_Wren.Best Ways to Identify:
Plain brown wren without bold face markings. Energetic
with cocked tail. Loud
bubbling song. Very common.

Northern_Jacana.Description:
Unusual wader. Dark chestnut body, black head and
neck, yellow frontal shield and bill, extremely
long toes. About 9 inches.
Northern_Jacana.Behavior:
Walks on floating vegetation using enormously long
toes. Polyandrous; female defends territory with
multiple males. Found in Texas and Caribbean.
Northern_Jacana.Habitat:
Freshwater ponds and marshes with floating vegetation
in southern Texas, Caribbean, and Central America.
Northern_Jacana.Similar Looking Birds:
No similar bird in range. Long toes and
chestnut coloring unique.
Northern_Jacana.Best Ways to Identify:
Chestnut body with black head and yellow bill/shield.
Walks on lily pads on enormous
toes. Unmistakable.

Northern_Lapwing.Description:
Large plover with long wispy black crest, iridescent
green-black upperparts, white underparts, orange
undertail. About 12 inches.
Northern_Lapwing.Behavior:
Tumbling display flights in spring. Forages for
earthworms and insects. Rare vagrant to northeastern
North America from Eurasia.
Northern_Lapwing.Habitat:
Farmland, meadows, and wetland edges in Eurasia.
Rare vagrant to Atlantic coast of North
America, especially after Atlantic storms.
Northern_Lapwing.Similar Looking Birds:
No other lapwing in North America. Crest and
iridescent plumage distinctive.
Northern_Lapwing.Best Ways to Identify:
Long wispy crest, iridescent green back, and black
and white plumage distinctive. Broad
rounded wings in flight.

Northern_Mockingbird.Description: Gray bird with white wing patches, white outer tail feathers, and long tail. Mimics dozens of species.
Northern_Mockingbird.Behavior: Sings at night during breeding season. Aggressively defends territory year-round.
Northern_Mockingbird.Habitat: Open areas with shrubs, gardens, and forest edges across North America.
Northern_Mockingbird.Similar Looking Birds: Gray Catbird is darker gray without white wing patches; Loggerhead Shrike has black mask.
Northern_Mockingbird.Best Ways to Identify: White wing patches flashed in display, long tail, and extraordinary mimicry of other birds.

Northern_Parula.Description: Tiny warbler with blue-gray back, yellow-green patch on back, yellow throat and breast with dark breast bands.
Northern_Parula.Behavior: Hangs upside down from branch tips foraging for insects. Nests in hanging lichens.
Northern_Parula.Habitat: Mature forests with hanging lichens or Spanish moss in eastern North America.
Northern_Parula.Similar Looking Birds: Tropical Parula lacks the dark breast bands and is more uniformly yellow below.
Northern_Parula.Best Ways to Identify: Tiny blue-gray warbler with yellow-green back patch and dark breast bands.

Northern_Pintail.Description: Elegant dabbling duck. Male has chocolate-brown head, white neck stripe, gray body, and long pin tail.
Northern_Pintail.Behavior: Very long-distance migrant. Dabbles in shallow water for seeds and invertebrates.
Northern_Pintail.Habitat: Wetlands, flooded fields, and lakes across North America.
Northern_Pintail.Similar Looking Birds: Male's long tail pin and white neck stripe are unmistakable. Female is elegant and slim.
Northern_Pintail.Best Ways to Identify: Male's long tail pin and white neck stripe -- most elegant and slender of dabbling ducks.

Northern_Pygmy-Owl.Description:
Tiny owl without ear tufts. Brown spotted plumage,
streaked below, false eyespots on nape.
About 7 inches.
Northern_Pygmy-Owl.Behavior:
Diurnal; hunts birds and insects. Presence revealed
by scolding mobbing birds. Western
mountain forest resident.
Northern_Pygmy-Owl.Habitat:
Mountain conifer and mixed forest of western North
America. Year-round resident from
Alaska to Central America.
Northern_Pygmy-Owl.Similar Looking Birds:
Ferruginous Pygmy-Owl found at lower elevations. Northern
Pygmy-Owl is mountain forest species.
Northern_Pygmy-Owl.Best Ways to Identify:
Tiny spotted owl, active by day. Long tail, false
eyespots on nape. Western mountain
forests.

Northern_Red_Bishop.Description:
Small bird. Breeding male brilliant red-orange with
black face, belly, and wings.
Female streaked brown. About 4.5 inches.
Northern_Red_Bishop.Behavior:
Males display from grass stems. Breeds in weedy fields
and marshes. Introduced and
established in California and Texas.
Northern_Red_Bishop.Habitat:
Weedy fields, marshes, and grasslands. Established
feral populations in California,
Texas, and Hawaii.
Northern_Red_Bishop.Similar Looking Birds:
Orange Bishop similar. No other small bird in range
has all-orange and black
combination.
Northern_Red_Bishop.Best Ways to Identify:
Male brilliant orange-red with black belly and face.
Breeding plumage unmistakable.
Established feral in California.

Northern_Rough-winged_Swallow.Description: Plain brown-backed swallow with dingy gray-brown throat and white belly. No white rump.
Northern_Rough-winged_Swallow.Behavior: Nests in burrows in earthen banks, under bridges, and in pipes. Usually solitary.
Northern_Rough-winged_Swallow.Habitat: Near streams, rivers, and lakes with exposed earthen banks.
Northern_Rough-winged_Swallow.Similar Looking Birds: Bank Swallow has sharp brown breast band; Rough-winged has graduated dingy throat.
Northern_Rough-winged_Swallow.Best Ways to Identify: Plain brown back, no white rump, and gradually dingy throat shading to white belly.

Northern_Saw-whet_Owl.Description: Tiny owl with round head, no ear tufts, bright yellow eyes, and streaked brown-and-white underparts.
Northern_Saw-whet_Owl.Behavior: Completely nocturnal. Calls persistently with a repeated whistled note in spring.
Northern_Saw-whet_Owl.Habitat: Coniferous and mixed forests across North America.
Northern_Saw-whet_Owl.Similar Looking Birds: Boreal Owl is slightly larger with spotted forehead; Saw-whet has streaked forehead.
Northern_Saw-whet_Owl.Best Ways to Identify: Tiny owl -- rounded head, yellow eyes, and streaked forehead, not spotted like Boreal.

Northern_Shoveler.Description: Distinctive duck with huge spatula-shaped bill, green head, chestnut sides, and white breast.
Northern_Shoveler.Behavior: Swings bill side to side to filter water for crustaceans and seeds.
Northern_Shoveler.Habitat: Freshwater marshes and lakes across North America.
Northern_Shoveler.Similar Looking Birds: Mallard has smaller bill; no other duck has such an enormous spatula-shaped bill.
Northern_Shoveler.Best Ways to Identify: Giant spatula-shaped bill used to filter-feed -- unmistakable identification feature.

Northern_Shrike.Description: Large gray-and-white shrike with black mask, hooked bill, and black wings with white patches.
Northern_Shrike.Behavior: Impales prey on thorns and barbed wire. Irrupts south from boreal forest in winter.
Northern_Shrike.Habitat: Open country and forest edges; irruptive winter visitor from boreal regions.
Northern_Shrike.Similar Looking Birds: Loggerhead Shrike is smaller with complete black mask; Northern Shrike has barred breast.
Northern_Shrike.Best Ways to Identify: Larger than Loggerhead, with barred breast and incomplete mask -- winter visitor from north.

Northern_Waterthrush.Description: Warbler with yellowish supercilium, heavily streaked yellow-buff underparts, and tail-bobbing behavior.
Northern_Waterthrush.Behavior: Walks along still water edges and flooded forest floors bobbing tail.
Northern_Waterthrush.Habitat: Still or slow-moving water in boreal forests; breeds in northern areas.
Northern_Waterthrush.Similar Looking Birds: Louisiana Waterthrush has white supercilium and buffy flanks; Northern has yellowish.
Northern_Waterthrush.Best Ways to Identify: Yellowish supercilium, streaked yellowish underparts, and preference for still water.

Northern_Wheatear.Description:
Small thrush-like bird, gray above, buff-white below,
bold black mask on male, white
rump. About 6 inches.
Northern_Wheatear.Behavior:
Perches upright on rocks, bobs and bows. Breeds
in rocky tundra in Alaska and
Canada. Long-distance migrant to Africa.
Northern_Wheatear.Habitat:
Rocky tundra and open ground in Alaska and northern
Canada. Migrates across oceans
to Africa.
Northern_Wheatear.Similar Looking Birds:
Other wheatears rare in North America. No other
bird has white rump combined
with gray-backed pattern.
Northern_Wheatear.Best Ways to Identify:
White rump conspicuous in flight. Gray above, black
mask. Bobs on rocky
tundra. Arctic breeder.

Northern_Yellow_(Yellow)_Warbler.Description:
Small warbler, bright yellow throughout, male with
chestnut streaks on breast, yellow
tail spots. About 5 inches.
Northern_Yellow_(Yellow)_Warbler.Behavior:
Active forager in willows and shrubs. Sings sweet-sweet-sweet
song. Common summer breeder.
Northern_Yellow_(Yellow)_Warbler.Habitat:
Willow thickets, streamside shrubs, and woodland
edges across North America. Common
migratory warbler.
Northern_Yellow_(Yellow)_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds:
Wilson's Warbler has black cap. Prothonotary Warbler
has gray wings. Yellow Warbler
has yellow tail spots.
Northern_Yellow_(Yellow)_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify:
Bright yellow throughout with chestnut streaks on
breast. Yellow spots in tail.
Willows and streamside shrubs.

Nuttalls_Woodpecker.Description: Small woodpecker with barred black-and-white back, white-spotted wings, and red nape on males.
Nuttalls_Woodpecker.Behavior: Forages on oaks for insects. Nearly identical to Ladder-backed Woodpecker.
Nuttalls_Woodpecker.Habitat: Oak woodlands and chaparral of California.
Nuttalls_Woodpecker.Similar Looking Birds: Ladder-backed Woodpecker is nearly identical but found in desert; ranges barely overlap.
Nuttalls_Woodpecker.Best Ways to Identify: California oak woodlands -- nearly identical to Ladder-backed but habitat separates them.

Nuttings_Flycatcher.Description:
Small Myiarchus flycatcher, very similar to Ash-throated.
Orange mouth lining and subtle
differences in tail rufous. About 7 inches.
Nuttings_Flycatcher.Behavior:
Mexican species occasionally recorded in southern
Arizona. Very rare vagrant; best identified
by call.
Nuttings_Flycatcher.Habitat:
Dry deciduous and thorn forest of Mexico. Very rare
vagrant to southern Arizona.
Nuttings_Flycatcher.Similar Looking Birds:
Ash-throated Flycatcher nearly identical. Best distinguished
by call; orange vs pale mouth lining.
Nuttings_Flycatcher.Best Ways to Identify:
Nearly identical to Ash-throated Flycatcher. Orange
mouth lining visible when calling.
Very rare Arizona vagrant.

Oahu_Akepa.Description:
Small Hawaiian honeycreeper, male orange-red with
slightly crossed bill tips.
Female olive. Extinct approximately 1900.
Oahu_Akepa.Behavior:
Used crossed bill to open flower buds for nectar.
Extinct from Oahu due to
deforestation and disease.
Oahu_Akepa.Similar Looking Birds:
Hawaii Akepa on Big Island. Akekee on Kauai. No
similar birds survive on Oahu.
Oahu_Akepa.Best Ways to Identify:
Extinct. Orange-red male, crossed bill. Oahu.
No longer exists.

Oahu_Akialoa.Description:
Small Hawaiian honeycreeper, very long decurved bill,
yellow-olive body. Extinct
since approximately 1837.
Oahu_Akialoa.Behavior:
Probed bark for insects and flowers for nectar.
Among earliest Hawaiian birds
documented after Western contact.
Oahu_Akialoa.Habitat:
Native forests of Oahu. Extinct due to early
deforestation after Western
contact.
Oahu_Akialoa.Similar Looking Birds:
Other akialoa on different islands. No similar long-billed
birds survive on Oahu.
Oahu_Akialoa.Best Ways to Identify:
Extinct. Long decurved bill, yellow-olive. Oahu.
One of earliest recorded extinctions
in Hawaii.

Oahu_Alauahio.Description:
Small Hawaiian creeper. Male yellow with greenish
back. Female olive-green above,
yellowish below. About 4.5 inches.
Oahu_Alauahio.Behavior:
Crept along branches searching bark for insects.
Extinct since approximately 1985.
Last confirmed records from Oahu.
Oahu_Alauahio.Habitat:
Native forests of Oahu. Extinct due to deforestation,
introduced predators, and avian
diseases.
Oahu_Alauahio.Similar Looking Birds:
Oahu Amakihi similar but has curved bill. Other
alauahio species on different
Hawaiian islands.
Oahu_Alauahio.Best Ways to Identify:
Extinct creeper from Oahu. Male yellow with green
back. No longer exists in
native forest.

Oahu_Amakihi.Description:
Small Hawaiian honeycreeper, bright yellow-green below,
olive-green above, curved bill.
About 4.5 inches.
Oahu_Amakihi.Behavior:
Active forager for nectar and insects. Shows some
resistance to avian malaria.
Oahu's most common native forest bird.
Oahu_Amakihi.Habitat:
Native and suburban forests of Oahu. Tolerates lower
elevations and some introduced
tree species.
Oahu_Amakihi.Similar Looking Birds:
Warbling White-eye has white eye ring. Hawaii Amakihi
on different island. Brighter
yellow than other amakihi.
Oahu_Amakihi.Best Ways to Identify:
Bright yellow-green underparts, curved bill on Oahu.
Often in native and suburban
trees. Common endemic.

Oahu_Elepaio.Description:
Small monarch flycatcher endemic to Oahu. Rusty-brown
above, white rump, whitish below.
Cocks tail upward. About 5 inches.
Oahu_Elepaio.Behavior:
Bold and inquisitive, will approach humans closely.
Forages actively for insects.
Important species in Hawaiian forest.
Oahu_Elepaio.Habitat:
Native forests of the Koolau and Waianae mountain
ranges on Oahu. Endangered due
to habitat loss and introduced predators.
Oahu_Elepaio.Similar Looking Birds:
Kauai and Hawaii Elepaio similar but island-specific.
No other small flycatcher in
Oahu native forest habitat.
Oahu_Elepaio.Best Ways to Identify:
Upward-cocked tail, rusty-brown tones on Oahu.
Distinctive white rump patch.
Endemic and endangered forest bird.

Oahu_Nukupuu.Description:
Small Hawaiian honeycreeper, long strongly decurved
bill, yellow male. Extinct since
approximately 1860.
Oahu_Nukupuu.Behavior:
Used long bill to probe bark for insects and nectar.
Extinct shortly after Western
contact with Hawaii.
Oahu_Nukupuu.Habitat:
Native forests of Oahu. Extinct due to early deforestation
and introduced species.
Oahu_Nukupuu.Similar Looking Birds:
Oahu Amakihi smaller with shorter bill. No similar
birds survive on Oahu.
Oahu_Nukupuu.Best Ways to Identify:
Extinct. Long decurved bill, yellow male. From Oahu.
No longer exists.

Oahu_Oo.Description:
Small black Hawaiian honeyeater with yellow shoulder
patches and undertail coverts.
Long bill. About 8 inches.
Oahu_Oo.Behavior:
Foraged for nectar in native Hawaiian forest.
Extinct since approximately 1837
due to early human impacts.
Oahu_Oo.Habitat:
Native forests of Oahu. Extinct due to habitat
loss following Polynesian and
later Western settlement.
Oahu_Oo.Similar Looking Birds:
Other Oo species similar but island-specific. All
Hawaiian Oo now extinct.
Oahu_Oo.Best Ways to Identify:
Extinct species from Oahu. Black with yellow
shoulder and undertail patches.
No longer exists.

Oak_Titmouse.Description: Plain gray titmouse with small crest and no distinctive markings. Short dark bill.
Oak_Titmouse.Behavior: Forages actively in oaks. California counterpart to Juniper Titmouse in the Great Basin.
Oak_Titmouse.Habitat: Oak woodlands of California and the Pacific slope.
Oak_Titmouse.Similar Looking Birds: Juniper Titmouse is nearly identical but found in juniper woodland; ranges barely overlap.
Oak_Titmouse.Best Ways to Identify: Plain gray with crest -- nearly identical to Juniper Titmouse but in California oak woodland.

Olive-backed_Pipit.Description:
Small pipit, olive-green back with little streaking,
white underparts with dark streaks,
bold supercilium. About 6 inches.
Olive-backed_Pipit.Behavior:
Forages on ground in forest and woodland edges.
Regular vagrant to western Alaska
and Aleutian Islands.
Olive-backed_Pipit.Habitat:
Forests and forest edges of Siberia and East Asia.
Regular vagrant to western Alaska.
Olive-backed_Pipit.Similar Looking Birds:
Pechora Pipit more heavily streaked above. Tree Pipit
less olive above. Red-throated
has brighter pink throat.
Olive-backed_Pipit.Best Ways to Identify:
Olive-green back with little streaking. Bold supercilium.
Regular Alaska vagrant in
fall migration.

Olive-sided_Flycatcher.Description: Large flycatcher with dark olive vest on sides, white central belly stripe, and white tufts on rump.
Olive-sided_Flycatcher.Behavior: Perches at treetops singing loud quick-THREE-beers. Long-distance migrant.
Olive-sided_Flycatcher.Habitat: Coniferous forests and burned areas with tall snags across western North America.
Olive-sided_Flycatcher.Similar Looking Birds: Wood-Pewees lack the dark vest; Olive-sided has distinctive vest and rump tufts.
Olive-sided_Flycatcher.Best Ways to Identify: Dark olive vest framing white belly, white rump tufts, and quick-THREE-beers song.

Olive_Sparrow.Description:
Medium sparrow, olive-green above, pale below, bold
brown crown stripes, no wing
bars. About 6 inches.
Olive_Sparrow.Behavior:
Forages on ground under dense brush by scratching
with both feet. Secretive.
Resident in south Texas.
Olive_Sparrow.Habitat:
Dense thorn scrub and brushy woodland of south
Texas and eastern Mexico.
Olive_Sparrow.Similar Looking Birds:
Green-tailed Towhee has rufous crown. Lincoln's Sparrow
streaked below. Olive color
distinctive.
Olive_Sparrow.Best Ways to Identify:
Olive-green above, plain below, bold crown stripes.
South Texas thorn scrub.
Ground-scratching forager.

Olive_Warbler.Description:
Medium wood warbler. Male has orange head with black
mask, olive-gray back, white
wing bars. About 5 inches.
Olive_Warbler.Behavior:
Forages high in pine canopy for insects. Mountain
specialist in Arizona and New
Mexico pine forests.
Olive_Warbler.Habitat:
High-elevation pine and mixed pine-oak forests of
Arizona, New Mexico, and Mexico.
Olive_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds:
Hermit Warbler has yellow head but no black mask.
Virginia's Warbler lacks orange
and mask.
Olive_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify:
Orange head with black mask unique. White wing bars.
High-elevation pine forest.
Arizona and New Mexico.

Olomao.Description:
Medium Hawaiian thrush, brown above with gray
underparts. Island endemic of
Lanai and Molokai. About 8 inches.
Olomao.Behavior:
Foraged for fruit in native forest. Very few
if any individuals likely remain.
Song melodious.
Olomao.Habitat:
Native forests of Lanai and Molokai. Lanai population
extinct; Molokai population
possibly persists.
Olomao.Similar Looking Birds:
Omao similar but on Big Island. Kamao similar
but Kauai only.
Olomao.Best Ways to Identify:
Possibly extinct Hawaiian thrush. Brown above, gray
below. Lanai and Molokai
native forest habitat.

Omao.Description:
Medium Hawaiian thrush, dark brown above, gray
below, white eye ring. Upright
posture. About 7 inches.
Omao.Behavior:
Forages for fruit and insects in native forest.
The most common surviving Hawaiian
thrush. Melodious song.
Omao.Habitat:
Native forests of the Big Island of Hawaii.
Found primarily above 4,000 feet
in ohia and koa forest.
Omao.Similar Looking Birds:
Puaiohi smaller with pink legs. Other Hawaiian
thrushes on different islands.
Omao.Best Ways to Identify:
White eye ring on dark brown thrush. Big Island
of Hawaii native forest.
Most common surviving Hawaiian thrush.

Orange-billed_Nightingale-Thrush.Description:
Small thrush, gray-brown above, gray below with
orange bill and orange eye ring.
About 6.5 inches.
Orange-billed_Nightingale-Thrush.Behavior:
Forages on ground in dense forest. Melodious song.
Rare vagrant to extreme southern
Texas from Mexico.
