with spotted breast and olive-brown
streaks on flanks. About 5 inches.
River_Warbler.Behavior:
Skulks in dense streamside vegetation. Distinctive
mechanical reeling song. Very rare
vagrant to North America.
River_Warbler.Habitat:
Dense riparian vegetation, forest edges, and scrub
in Europe and Asia. Very rare
vagrant to North America.
River_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds:
Savi's Warbler similar but unstreaked below. Marsh
Warbler and Reed Warbler
lack streaked flanks.
River_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify:
Spotted breast, streaked olive-brown flanks, plain
brown back. Skulking behavior.
Very rare vagrant from Europe.

Rivolis_Hummingbird.Description:
Large hummingbird. Male has brilliant iridescent purple
crown, emerald-green throat, dark body. Female
dull green above, spotted gray below. About 5 inches.
Rivolis_Hummingbird.Behavior:
Feeds on nectar; defends feeding territories aggressively.
Hovers with slow wingbeats for large size.
Found in mountain canyons of Southwest.
Rivolis_Hummingbird.Habitat:
Mountain pine-oak and riparian canyons of Arizona,
New Mexico, and west Texas. Also Mexico
and Central America.
Rivolis_Hummingbird.Similar Looking Birds:
Blue-throated Mountain-gem shares similar habitat.
Male Rivoli's purple crown and green throat unique.
Rivolis_Hummingbird.Best Ways to Identify:
Male's purple crown and emerald-green throat iridescent
in good light. Large size among
hummingbirds. Mountain canyon habitat in Southwest.

Roadside_Hawk.Description:
Small hawk, gray-brown above with rufous barring below,
gray head, yellow eyes.
About 14 inches.
Roadside_Hawk.Behavior:
Common hawk of roadsides and forest edges in Mexico
and Central America. Rare vagrant
to southern Texas.
Roadside_Hawk.Habitat:
Forest edges, roadsides, and open areas from Mexico
to Argentina. Rare vagrant to
southern Texas.
Roadside_Hawk.Similar Looking Birds:
Broad-winged Hawk similar but larger with different
tail pattern.
Roadside_Hawk.Best Ways to Identify:
Small hawk with rufous barring below, gray head.
Commonly perches on roadside wires
and posts. Rare Texas vagrant.

Rock_Dove.Description: Familiar pigeon with blue-gray plumage, iridescent neck, two black wing bars, and white rump; variable plumage.
Rock_Dove.Behavior: Highly adaptable; eats seeds and scraps; nests on building ledges; coos softly; flocks in urban areas.
Rock_Dove.Habitat: Cities, towns, farms, and cliff faces worldwide; originally cliff-dwelling species from Eurasia and North Africa.
Rock_Dove.Similar Looking Birds: Band-tailed Pigeon is larger with yellow bill tip and band across tail; Eurasian Collared-Dove has collar.
Rock_Dove.Best Ways to Identify: White rump in flight; two black wing bars; iridescent neck; feral urban pigeon; variable color morphs common.

Rock_Ptarmigan.Description: Grouse with all-white winter plumage, black eye stripe through eye, and feathered feet.
Rock_Ptarmigan.Behavior: Turns white in winter for camouflage in snow. Males retain black eye stripe.
Rock_Ptarmigan.Habitat: Arctic and alpine tundra across northern North America.
Rock_Ptarmigan.Similar Looking Birds: Willow Ptarmigan is larger and lacks black eye stripe in winter; Rock has black stripe.
Rock_Ptarmigan.Best Ways to Identify: All-white winter plumage with black eye stripe -- camouflaged in alpine and Arctic tundra.

Rock_Sandpiper.Description: Medium shorebird; breeding plumage has rufous back, gray head, and black belly patch; dull gray in winter.
Rock_Sandpiper.Behavior: Forages on wave-washed rocky shores and kelp beds; tame and approachable; winters on rocky Pacific coasts.
Rock_Sandpiper.Habitat: Breeds on tundra and rocky coasts of Alaska; winters on rocky shorelines of Pacific Coast south to California.
Rock_Sandpiper.Similar Looking Birds: Purple Sandpiper is Atlantic counterpart; Dunlin is smaller without black belly patch in breeding plumage.
Rock_Sandpiper.Best Ways to Identify: Rocky shoreline habitat; black belly patch in summer; yellowish legs; drooped bill tip; stocky chunky build.

Rock_Wren.Description: Sandy-gray wren with finely spotted back, buffy rump, and rufous tail corners. Bobs body constantly.
Rock_Wren.Behavior: Bobs its body up and down constantly. Paves nest entrance with small flat stones.
Rock_Wren.Habitat: Rocky slopes, cliffs, and dry canyon walls across western North America.
Rock_Wren.Similar Looking Birds: Canyon Wren has white throat and rufous body; Rock Wren is sandy-gray throughout.
Rock_Wren.Best Ways to Identify: Sandy-gray with spotted back, constant body bobbing, and rocky habitat in the west.

Rose-breasted_Grosbeak.Description: Male has black head, white underparts, brilliant rose-red triangular breast patch, and large white bill.
Rose-breasted_Grosbeak.Behavior: Rich warbling song. Males share incubation duties. Visits backyard feeders.
Rose-breasted_Grosbeak.Habitat: Deciduous forests and forest edges of eastern North America.
Rose-breasted_Grosbeak.Similar Looking Birds: Black-headed Grosbeak male has orange breast; Rose-breasted male has rose-red triangle.
Rose-breasted_Grosbeak.Best Ways to Identify: Male's rose-red triangle on white breast is unmistakable -- visits backyard feeders.

Rose-ringed_Parakeet.Description:
Slender green parakeet, long pointed tail. Male has
black and rose-pink collar ring.
About 16 inches including tail.
Rose-ringed_Parakeet.Behavior:
Established feral populations worldwide. Flocks in
parks and suburbs. Noisy. Feral in
Florida and California.
Rose-ringed_Parakeet.Habitat:
Feral in Florida, California, and many worldwide cities.
Native to Africa and
South Asia.
Rose-ringed_Parakeet.Similar Looking Birds:
Monk Parakeet shorter tail and gray breast. Rose-ringed
has very long tail.
Rose-ringed_Parakeet.Best Ways to Identify:
Very long pointed tail. Male has rose-pink neck ring.
Green. Feral in Florida and
California cities.

Rose-throated_Becard.Description:
Medium bird, male gray with black cap and rose-pink
throat. Female brown with gray cap
and buff underparts. About 7 inches.
Rose-throated_Becard.Behavior:
Builds large globular hanging nest. Regular rare summer
visitor to southeastern Arizona
riparian canyons.
Rose-throated_Becard.Similar Looking Birds:
Gray-collared Becard lacks pink throat. Rose-throated
Becard male's pink throat distinctive.
Rose-throated_Becard.Best Ways to Identify:
Male: rose-pink throat patch. Female: brown with buff
underparts. Builds hanging nest.
Arizona riparian canyons.

Roseate_Spoonbill.Description: Pink bird with spatula-shaped bill, naked yellow-green head, and red shoulder bar.
Roseate_Spoonbill.Behavior: Swings spoon-shaped bill side to side in water to capture small fish and invertebrates.
Roseate_Spoonbill.Habitat: Coastal marshes and mangroves of the Gulf Coast and Florida.
Roseate_Spoonbill.Similar Looking Birds: Flamingo is deeper pink and taller; Spoonbill has spatula bill and shorter stature.
Roseate_Spoonbill.Best Ways to Identify: Pink plumage and spatula-shaped bill -- unmistakable wading bird of Gulf Coast marshes.

Roseate_Tern.Description: Slender white tern with pale gray back, black cap, deeply forked tail with long outer streamers, and dark bill.
Roseate_Tern.Behavior: Dives for small fish; colonial nester; gives harsh grating calls; associates with Common and Arctic Terns.
Roseate_Tern.Habitat: Coastal islands and beaches; breeds in small colonies on rocky or sandy islands in northeastern US and tropics.
Roseate_Tern.Similar Looking Birds: Common Tern has orange-red bill base; Arctic Tern has all-red bill; both have shorter tail streamers.
Roseate_Tern.Best Ways to Identify: Extremely long tail streamers beyond wings at rest; mostly dark bill; pale whitish underparts with rosy flush.

Ross_Goose.Description: Small stocky white goose with black wingtips; tiny stubby pink bill with bluish-gray warty base; round head.
Ross_Goose.Behavior: Migrates in large flocks with Snow Geese; grazes on grain fields; breeds on tundra in Arctic Canada.
Ross_Goose.Habitat: Arctic tundra for breeding; winters in Central Valley of California, Gulf Coast, and interior agricultural fields.
Ross_Goose.Similar Looking Birds: Snow Goose is larger with longer bill showing grinning patch; blue morph Snow Goose is similar to blue morph Ross.
Ross_Goose.Best Ways to Identify: Tiny bill without grinning patch; small rounded head; smaller overall than Snow Goose; stubby pink bill.

Rosss_Gull.Description:
Small Arctic gull. Breeding adult has rosy-pink
flush on white plumage, thin black collar, wedge-
shaped tail. About 13 inches.
Rosss_Gull.Behavior:
Breeds at high Arctic latitudes; rarely seen south.
Irregular winter visitor to northern Atlantic and
Pacific coasts.
Rosss_Gull.Habitat:
High Arctic tundra and sea ice. Irregular winter
visitor to northeastern North America. Very rare
south of Arctic.
Rosss_Gull.Similar Looking Birds:
Bonaparte's Gull similar size. Ross's has wedge-
shaped tail and pink flush.
Rosss_Gull.Best Ways to Identify:
Wedge-shaped tail distinctive. Pink flush on white
plumage. Thin black collar.
Rare Arctic visitor.

Rosy-faced_Lovebird.Description:
Small stocky parrot, bright green with rosy-pink face
and throat, blue rump.
About 6 inches.
Rosy-faced_Lovebird.Behavior:
Established feral population in Phoenix area, Arizona.
Nests in cactus and buildings.
Popular cage bird.
Rosy-faced_Lovebird.Habitat:
Established feral population in Phoenix, Arizona suburban
areas. Native to southwestern
Africa.
Rosy-faced_Lovebird.Similar Looking Birds:
No other parrot in Arizona has rosy-pink face. Unique
in range.
Rosy-faced_Lovebird.Best Ways to Identify:
Rosy-pink face, green body, blue rump. Small stocky
parrot. Feral in Phoenix, Arizona.
Unique in North America.

Rough-legged_Hawk.Description: Large buteo with feathered legs, dark belly band, and pale tail with broad dark terminal band.
Rough-legged_Hawk.Behavior: Hovers while hunting voles over open fields. Irrupts south from Arctic in winter.
Rough-legged_Hawk.Habitat: Open tundra in summer; fields and marshes in winter across North America.
Rough-legged_Hawk.Similar Looking Birds: Ferruginous Hawk has rusty back; Rough-legged has feathered tarsi and distinct belly band.
Rough-legged_Hawk.Best Ways to Identify: Feathered legs, distinctive dark belly, and hovering flight over open fields in winter.

Royal_Tern.Description: Large orange-billed tern with black cap (often showing white forehead in non-breeding), and deeply forked tail.
Royal_Tern.Behavior: Plunge-dives for fish in coastal waters. Nests in dense colonies on beaches.
Royal_Tern.Habitat: Atlantic and Pacific coasts and Gulf of Mexico.
Royal_Tern.Similar Looking Birds: Caspian Tern is larger with red bill; Elegant Tern is slimmer with longer curved bill.
Royal_Tern.Best Ways to Identify: Large tern with bright orange bill -- often shows white forehead outside breeding season.

Ruby-crowned_Kinglet.Description: Tiny olive-green bird with bold white eye ring, two white wing bars, and hidden red crown on male.
Ruby-crowned_Kinglet.Behavior: Constantly flicks wings while foraging. Huge song for its tiny size.
Ruby-crowned_Kinglet.Habitat: Coniferous forests; widespread migrant in shrubs and forests.
Ruby-crowned_Kinglet.Similar Looking Birds: Golden-crowned Kinglet has striped head; Ruby-crowned has bold eye ring.
Ruby-crowned_Kinglet.Best Ways to Identify: Bold white eye ring, constant wing-flicking, and huge bubbling song from tiny bird.

Ruby-throated_Hummingbird.Description: Male has brilliant iridescent ruby-red throat, green back, and white underparts. Tiny size.
Ruby-throated_Hummingbird.Behavior: Only hummingbird regularly nesting in eastern North America. Migrates across Gulf of Mexico.
Ruby-throated_Hummingbird.Habitat: Gardens, forest edges, and flowering areas across eastern North America.
Ruby-throated_Hummingbird.Similar Looking Birds: Black-chinned Hummingbird is the western counterpart; Ruby-throated is eastern.
Ruby-throated_Hummingbird.Best Ways to Identify: Male's iridescent ruby-red throat -- the only hummingbird nesting throughout eastern North America.

Ruddy_Duck.Description: Small stiff-tailed duck. Breeding male has bright blue bill, rufous body, black cap, and white cheek.
Ruddy_Duck.Behavior: Holds stiff tail cocked up when alert. Rarely walks on land.
Ruddy_Duck.Habitat: Open water, lakes, and coastal bays across North America.
Ruddy_Duck.Similar Looking Birds: Masked Duck is rare; Ruddy Duck male's blue bill and white cheek are distinctive.
Ruddy_Duck.Best Ways to Identify: Bright blue bill, white cheek, and stiff cocked tail on breeding male.

Ruddy_Ground_Dove.Description:
Small dove. Male reddish-brown with blue-gray head.
Female grayish-brown. Dark spots on wings.
About 7 inches.
Ruddy_Ground_Dove.Behavior:
Forages for seeds on ground in pairs or small groups.
Common and approachable in its range.
Resident in Mexico; rare visitor to southern US.
Ruddy_Ground_Dove.Habitat:
Open areas, farms, gardens, and roadsides in
tropical lowlands. Rare visitor to southern
California, Arizona, and Texas.
Ruddy_Ground_Dove.Similar Looking Birds:
Common Ground Dove similar. Male Ruddy is richer
reddish-brown with blue-gray head.
Ruddy_Ground_Dove.Best Ways to Identify:
Male's deep reddish-rust plumage and blue-gray head.
Dark wing spots. Smaller and
richer-colored than Common Ground Dove.

Ruddy_Quail-Dove.Description:
Small chunky dove. Male rich reddish-brown with
purple gloss, pale face stripe, iridescent neck.
Female duller brown. About 9 inches.
Ruddy_Quail-Dove.Behavior:
Walks quietly on forest floor seeking seeds and
fallen fruit. Very secretive. Rare visitor
to Florida Keys from Caribbean.
Ruddy_Quail-Dove.Habitat:
Dense tropical forest understory in Caribbean and
Central America. Rarely seen in Florida
in dense subtropical growth.
Ruddy_Quail-Dove.Similar Looking Birds:
Key West Quail-Dove has distinct bold white
face stripe.
Ruddy_Quail-Dove.Best Ways to Identify:
Male's rich rufous-brown plumage with pale facial
stripe and purplish sheen. Found
walking on dense forest floor.

Ruddy_Shelduck.Description:
Large duck-goose, bright orange-rufous body, pale
head, black tail and wingtips,
white wing patches. About 26 inches.
Ruddy_Shelduck.Behavior:
Forages on grasslands and wetlands. Most sightings
in North America likely escaped
birds. Rare vagrant.
Ruddy_Shelduck.Habitat:
Wetlands, grasslands, and river valleys of Europe
and Asia. Rare vagrant to
North America; most records questionable.
Ruddy_Shelduck.Similar Looking Birds:
No similar orange-rufous duck in North America. White
wing patches distinctive in
flight.
Ruddy_Shelduck.Best Ways to Identify:
Bright orange-rufous body with pale head. White wing
patches in flight. Likely
escaped from captivity in most cases.

Ruddy_Turnstone.Description: Stocky shorebird with bold harlequin pattern of rusty-red, black, and white. Short orange legs.
Ruddy_Turnstone.Behavior: Flips pebbles and shells to find invertebrates underneath. Bold and approachable.
Ruddy_Turnstone.Habitat: Rocky and sandy shores and mudflats along coasts during migration.
Ruddy_Turnstone.Similar Looking Birds: Black Turnstone has all-dark face; Ruddy Turnstone has complex rusty-and-black pattern.
Ruddy_Turnstone.Best Ways to Identify: Bold rusty, black, and white pattern and habit of flipping stones on rocky shores.

Ruff.Description:
Unusual sandpiper with variable plumage. Breeding
male has elaborate neck ruff and head tufts in
variable colors. Female (reeve) smaller and plain. About 12 inches.
Ruff.Behavior:
Males display at leks with spectacular ruff plumage.
Rare but regular vagrant to North America
from Eurasia. Forages in fields and wetlands.
Ruff.Habitat:
Breeds on Eurasian wet meadows. Winters in Africa.
Uncommon but regular vagrant to
North America.
Ruff.Similar Looking Birds:
Buff-breasted Sandpiper similar in non-breeding. Breeding
male's elaborate ruff unmistakable.
Ruff.Best Ways to Identify:
Breeding male's colorful neck ruff unmistakable. Non-
breeding birds scaly-backed with small
head and drooping bill tip.

Ruffed_Grouse.Description:
Medium-sized grouse with brown or gray mottled
plumage, fan-shaped tail with dark terminal band,
and feathered neck ruff. About 17 inches.
Ruffed_Grouse.Behavior:
Male drums on logs by beating wings rapidly.
Explodes into flight when flushed. Feeds on
buds, leaves, berries, and insects seasonally.
Ruffed_Grouse.Habitat:
Mixed deciduous and coniferous forests with young
aspen stands. Common across northern and
eastern North America's forested areas.
Ruffed_Grouse.Similar Looking Birds:
Spruce Grouse in boreal forests. Sharp-tailed Grouse
in more open areas.
Ruffed_Grouse.Best Ways to Identify:
Fan tail with dark subterminal band. Male's neck
ruff visible when displaying. Explosive
wing thunder when flushed.

Rufous-backed_Robin.Description:
Medium thrush with deep rufous-orange back, gray
head, white throat with streaks,
orange bill. About 9.5 inches.
Rufous-backed_Robin.Behavior:
Forages for fruit in forest understory. Rare but
regular winter vagrant to Arizona
and New Mexico from Mexico.
Rufous-backed_Robin.Habitat:
Forest and scrub of western Mexico. Rare winter
visitor to Arizona and New Mexico
canyons.
Rufous-backed_Robin.Similar Looking Birds:
American Robin has red breast not rufous back.
Clay-colored Thrush all dull
brown without rufous tones.
Rufous-backed_Robin.Best Ways to Identify:
Bright rufous-orange back contrasting with gray head.
Arizona/New Mexico winter vagrant.
Orange bill. Streaked white throat.

Rufous-capped_Warbler.Description:
Medium warbler, rufous crown and cheeks, white supercilium,
olive-green above, bright
yellow underparts. About 5 inches.
Rufous-capped_Warbler.Behavior:
Forages low in dense scrub and understory. Cocks
and pumps tail. Rare vagrant to
Arizona and Texas from Mexico.
Rufous-capped_Warbler.Habitat:
Dense scrub and second growth in mountains of Mexico.
Rare vagrant to Arizona
and Texas.
Rufous-capped_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds:
No similar bird with rufous cap and cheeks plus
yellow underparts in range.
Rufous-capped_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify:
Rufous cap and cheeks distinctive. White supercilium.
Bright yellow below. Rare
Arizona and Texas vagrant.

Rufous-collared_Sparrow.Description:
Medium sparrow, gray head with black stripes, rufous
collar, streaked brown back.
About 6 inches.
Rufous-collared_Sparrow.Behavior:
Forages on ground. One of commonest birds in South
America. Very rare vagrant
to Texas and Florida.
Rufous-collared_Sparrow.Habitat:
Open areas, roadsides, and gardens throughout Central
and South America. Very rare
vagrant to North America.
Rufous-collared_Sparrow.Similar Looking Birds:
White-crowned Sparrow lacks rufous collar. Chipping
Sparrow has rusty cap.
Rufous collar distinctive.
Rufous-collared_Sparrow.Best Ways to Identify:
Rufous collar distinctive. Gray-striped head. Very
rare vagrant from Central and
South America.

Rufous-crowned_Sparrow.Description: Brown sparrow with rufous crown, gray face, single black malar stripe, and plain gray underparts.
Rufous-crowned_Sparrow.Behavior: Stays close to the ground in rocky scrub. Rarely flies far when disturbed.
Rufous-crowned_Sparrow.Habitat: Rocky slopes with sparse grass and shrubs in the southwestern United States.
Rufous-crowned_Sparrow.Similar Looking Birds: Chipping Sparrow has white supercilium and black eye line; Rufous-crowned has malar stripe.
Rufous-crowned_Sparrow.Best Ways to Identify: Rufous cap, gray face, single black malar stripe on rocky southwestern slopes.

Rufous-necked_Wood-Rail.Description:
Large rail. Rufous-orange head and neck, gray back
and wings, black and white barred flanks, red
legs and bill. About 11 inches.
Rufous-necked_Wood-Rail.Behavior:
Walks and forages in mangroves and forest edges.
Loud calls at dusk. Very rare vagrant to
Texas from Mexico and Central America.
Rufous-necked_Wood-Rail.Habitat:
Mangroves and coastal forest in Mexico and Central
America. Very rare vagrant to southern
Texas.
Rufous-necked_Wood-Rail.Similar Looking Birds:
Other wood-rails in neotropics. Rufous neck and
gray body combination distinctive.
Rufous-necked_Wood-Rail.Best Ways to Identify:
Rufous-orange head and neck contrasting with gray
body. Red legs and bill. Very rare
vagrant in Texas mangroves.

Rufous-tailed_Robin.Description:
Small chat-flycatcher, olive-brown above with rusty-rufous
rump and tail, scaly-spotted
breast. About 5 inches.
Rufous-tailed_Robin.Behavior:
Skulks in dense low cover. Sings loud rising whistle.
Very rare vagrant to western
Alaska from Asia.
Rufous-tailed_Robin.Habitat:
Dense forest and scrub undergrowth of East Asia.
Very rare vagrant to western
Alaska.
Rufous-tailed_Robin.Similar Looking Birds:
Siberian Blue Robin male brilliant blue. Taiga
Flycatcher sits more upright.
Rufous tail distinctive.
Rufous-tailed_Robin.Best Ways to Identify:
Rufous-orange tail contrasting with brown body.
Scaly spots on breast. Very
rare Alaska vagrant from Asia.

Rufous-tailed_Rock-Thrush.Description:
Medium thrush. Male blue head and back, orange-red
underparts and tail. Female brown
with scaled pattern. About 7.5 inches.
Rufous-tailed_Rock-Thrush.Behavior:
Perches on rocks and boulders. Sings from exposed
rocky perch. Very rare vagrant
to North America from Europe.
Rufous-tailed_Rock-Thrush.Habitat:
Rocky mountain slopes and open woodland in Europe
and Asia. Very rare vagrant
to North America.
Rufous-tailed_Rock-Thrush.Similar Looking Birds:
Blue Rock-Thrush male all blue without orange underparts.
No similar bird in
North America.
Rufous-tailed_Rock-Thrush.Best Ways to Identify:
Male blue head with orange-red underparts and tail.
Female scaled brown. Very
rare European vagrant.

Rufous-winged_Sparrow.Description: Small sparrow with rufous-edged wing coverts forming orange shoulder patch; gray face with two black malar stripes.
Rufous-winged_Sparrow.Behavior: Sings from tall cactus or shrub after summer rains; forages on ground for seeds; rare and local in range.
Rufous-winged_Sparrow.Habitat: Desert grassland with mixed grasses and thorny shrubs in southern Arizona near Mexican border.
Rufous-winged_Sparrow.Similar Looking Birds: Rufous-crowned Sparrow lacks double malar stripe; Botteri's Sparrow is browner with different face pattern.
Rufous-winged_Sparrow.Best Ways to Identify: Two black whisker stripes; rufous shoulder patch; flat gray head with rufous lateral crown stripe; desert grass.

Rufous_Hummingbird.Description: Male is entirely bright rufous-orange with iridescent red-orange throat and small white breast patch.
Rufous_Hummingbird.Behavior: Fiercely defends feeders and flowers. Makes one of the longest migrations relative to body size.
Rufous_Hummingbird.Habitat: Open forests, meadows, and gardens; breeds from the Pacific Northwest to Alaska.
Rufous_Hummingbird.Similar Looking Birds: Allen's Hummingbird is nearly identical but has green back; Rufous male is all rufous.
Rufous_Hummingbird.Best Ways to Identify: All-rufous male -- the most aggressive hummingbird at feeders.

Rustic_Bunting.Description:
Medium bunting. Male has black head, white supercilium,
chestnut breast band, white
belly. Female streaked. About 6 inches.
Rustic_Bunting.Behavior:
Forages on ground in woodland. Regular vagrant to
western Alaska and Aleutian
Islands from Siberia.
Rustic_Bunting.Habitat:
Moist forest and scrub of northern Siberia. Regular
vagrant to western Alaska.
Rustic_Bunting.Similar Looking Birds:
Reed Bunting male has black throat. Yellow-throated
Bunting has yellow. White
belly with chestnut band distinctive.
Rustic_Bunting.Best Ways to Identify:
Male black head, white supercilium, chestnut breast
band. Regular fall vagrant
to Aleutian Islands.

Rusty_Blackbird.Description: Medium blackbird; male glossy black with pale yellow eye; female grayish; both show rusty edges in fresh fall plumage.
Rusty_Blackbird.Behavior: Forages in wet woodland edges flipping leaf litter; declining significantly; migrates in mixed blackbird flocks.
Rusty_Blackbird.Habitat: Boreal bogs and wet forests for breeding; swampy woodlands, flooded fields, and wet thickets in winter.
Rusty_Blackbird.Similar Looking Birds: Brewer's Blackbird has purplish gloss and rounder head; Common Grackle has longer keel-shaped tail.
Rusty_Blackbird.Best Ways to Identify: Rusty feather edges in fall; pale yellow eye; wet woodland habitat; short tail; creaking squeaky vocalizations.

Sabines_Gull.Description:
Small gull with forked tail. Breeding adult has
dark gray hood, yellow-tipped black bill, bold
black and white and gray wing triangle. About 13 inches.
Sabines_Gull.Behavior:
Picks food from surface like a phalarope. Migrates
offshore. Regular pelagic migrant on both coasts
in fall.
Sabines_Gull.Habitat:
Breeds on Arctic tundra. Pelagic migrant offshore.
Regular fall migrant off both coasts.
Sabines_Gull.Similar Looking Birds:
Bonaparte's Gull similar size. Sabine's has forked
tail and striking wing pattern.
Sabines_Gull.Best Ways to Identify:
Striking black, white, and gray wing triangle in
flight. Forked tail. Pelagic migrant
visible offshore.

Saffron_Finch.Description:
Medium finch, brilliant yellow throughout, male with
orange forehead. Female yellowish-
green. About 5.5 inches.
Saffron_Finch.Behavior:
Gregarious in flocks, forages for seeds. Bold in
gardens. Introduced to Hawaii
and Puerto Rico.
Saffron_Finch.Habitat:
Open areas, gardens, and grasslands. Introduced to
Hawaii and Puerto Rico. Native
to South America.
Saffron_Finch.Similar Looking Birds:
Yellow-fronted Canary smaller and streaked. American
Goldfinch has black wings.
Brilliant yellow throughout distinctive.
Saffron_Finch.Best Ways to Identify:
Brilliant yellow throughout with orange forehead on
male. Introduced to Hawaii.
Gregarious seed-eater in open areas.

Sage_Grouse.Description: Large grouse; male has black belly, white breast rosette, spiky tail, and yellow air sacs; female mottled brown.
Sage_Grouse.Behavior: Males display on leks with popping air sac sounds; forages almost exclusively on sagebrush leaves and buds.
Sage_Grouse.Habitat: Sagebrush steppe of western North America; strictly dependent on big sagebrush for food and cover.
Sage_Grouse.Similar Looking Birds: Gunnison Sage-Grouse is smaller and found only in southwest Colorado; Sharp-tailed Grouse has different tail.
Sage_Grouse.Best Ways to Identify: Large size; spiky pointed tail; male's filoplume plumes on neck; black belly; sagebrush habitat association.

Sage_Sparrow.Description: Medium sparrow with gray head, white supercilium, single dark breast spot, brown streaked back, and dark malar stripe.
Sage_Sparrow.Behavior: Runs on ground with tail cocked; sings from sagebrush tops; pumps tail while walking; reluctant to fly.
Sage_Sparrow.Habitat: Sagebrush flats and alkali scrub of Great Basin; interior subspecies now considered separate species from coastal.
Sage_Sparrow.Similar Looking Birds: Bell's Sparrow is coastal and darker; Black-throated Sparrow lacks breast spot; Brewer's Sparrow more streaked.
Sage_Sparrow.Best Ways to Identify: Single dark breast spot; gray head; white eye-ring; tail-pumping behavior; sagebrush habitat; dark malar mark.

Sage_Thrasher.Description: Small pale thrasher with streaked underparts, short bill, white wing bars, and yellow eye.
Sage_Thrasher.Behavior: Sings from sagebrush perches. Runs on the ground between shrubs.
Sage_Thrasher.Habitat: Sagebrush flats of the Great Basin and Rocky Mountain foothills.
Sage_Thrasher.Similar Looking Birds: Curve-billed and Brown Thrashers have longer bills; Sage Thrasher is smallest with short bill.
Sage_Thrasher.Best Ways to Identify: Smallest thrasher -- streaked underparts, short bill, and white wing bars in sagebrush.

Sagebrush_Sparrow.Description: Gray-headed sparrow with white eye ring, single malar stripe, and plain white underparts with breast spot.
Sagebrush_Sparrow.Behavior: Runs with tail cocked. Rarely flies more than a short distance.
Sagebrush_Sparrow.Habitat: Dense sagebrush of the Great Basin.
Sagebrush_Sparrow.Similar Looking Birds: Bell's Sparrow is almost identical but found in coastal California chaparral.
Sagebrush_Sparrow.Best Ways to Identify: White eye ring, single malar stripe, and central breast spot in Great Basin sagebrush.

Saltmarsh_Sparrow.Description:
Small sparrow, orange-buff face triangle, streaked
breast and sides, flat head.
About 5 inches.
Saltmarsh_Sparrow.Behavior:
Skulks in dense saltmarsh grass. Nests at high tide
level, flooding nests periodically.
Extremely difficult to see.
Saltmarsh_Sparrow.Habitat:
Dense saltmarsh grass along Atlantic Coast from Maine
to Virginia. Strictly saltmarsh
specialist.
Saltmarsh_Sparrow.Similar Looking Birds:
Nelson's Sparrow more orange overall. Seaside Sparrow
darker gray. Orange face
triangle helpful.
Saltmarsh_Sparrow.Best Ways to Identify:
Orange-buff face triangle, streaked below. Dense saltmarsh
specialist along Atlantic Coast.
Flat head, secretive.

Salvins_Albatross.Description:
Medium mollymawk albatross. Gray head and neck, dark
back, white body, pale grayish bill with
yellow sides. About 37 inches.
Salvins_Albatross.Behavior:
Breeds on Bounty and Snares Islands, New Zealand.
Very rare vagrant to North American
Pacific coast.
Salvins_Albatross.Habitat:
Southern Pacific Ocean. Very rare vagrant to North
American Pacific coast, mostly
off California.
Salvins_Albatross.Similar Looking Birds:
White-capped Albatross has whiter head. Salvin's has
grayish head and pale gray bill.
Salvins_Albatross.Best Ways to Identify:
Grayish head with pale gray bill. Medium albatross.
Very rare Pacific vagrant from
New Zealand subantarctic.

Sanderling.Description: Small pale sandpiper that chases wave edges on sandy beaches. Has black shoulder spot and pale gray back.
Sanderling.Behavior: Runs back and forth following waves on sandy ocean beaches, probing wet sand.
Sanderling.Habitat: Sandy ocean beaches and mudflats during migration; Arctic tundra for breeding.
Sanderling.Similar Looking Birds: Dunlin is darker; Sanderling is palest small sandpiper and lacks hind toe.
Sanderling.Best Ways to Identify: Palest small sandpiper -- chases waves on sandy beaches, no hind toe.

Sandhill_Crane.Description: Tall gray bird with red forehead patch, white cheeks, and bustle of drooping rump feathers; long legs and neck.
Sandhill_Crane.Behavior: Bugling calls heard from great distances; dances in courtship; migrates in large flocks; omnivorous forager.
Sandhill_Crane.Habitat: Prairies, marshes, grain fields, and tundra; huge concentrations at Platte River Nebraska during spring migration.
Sandhill_Crane.Similar Looking Birds: Whooping Crane is white with red and black head; Great Blue Heron folds neck in flight; cranes fly with neck extended.
Sandhill_Crane.Best Ways to Identify: Gray plumage; red forehead; bustle of drooping feathers over rump; neck extended in flight; bugling calls.

Sandwich_Tern.Description: Medium-large tern with black bill with yellow tip, shaggy black crest, and pale gray upperparts.
Sandwich_Tern.Behavior: Plunge-dives for fish. Nests in colonies often with Royal Terns.
Sandwich_Tern.Habitat: Atlantic and Gulf coasts of North America.
Sandwich_Tern.Similar Looking Birds: Royal Tern has orange bill; Elegant has long curved bill; Sandwich has black bill with yellow tip.
Sandwich_Tern.Best Ways to Identify: Black bill with yellow tip and shaggy crest -- combination unique among North American terns.

Sargasso_Shearwater.Description:
Small shearwater, dark brown above, white below with
some brown on sides. Tropical Atlantic
species. About 11 inches.
Sargasso_Shearwater.Behavior:
Breeds on Caribbean and Atlantic islands. Forages
in tropical Atlantic; rare vagrant
to North American Atlantic coast.
Sargasso_Shearwater.Habitat:
Tropical North Atlantic. Rare vagrant to North American
Atlantic coast.
Sargasso_Shearwater.Similar Looking Birds:
Audubon's Shearwater nearly identical. Sargasso represents
Atlantic population previously lumped.
Sargasso_Shearwater.Best Ways to Identify:
Small dark-brown shearwater with white below. Tropical
Atlantic. Distinguished from Audubon's
by range and subtle details.

Savannah_Sparrow.Description: Small streaked sparrow with yellow supercilium, notched tail, and variable streaking. Short tail.
Savannah_Sparrow.Behavior: Abundant and widespread. Sings buzzy insect-like song from low perches in grass.
Savannah_Sparrow.Habitat: Open habitats including grasslands, marshes, and fields across North America.
Savannah_Sparrow.Similar Looking Birds: Song Sparrow has longer tail and central breast spot; Savannah is shorter-tailed with notch.
Savannah_Sparrow.Best Ways to Identify: Yellow supercilium, notched short tail, and buzzy song -- most common open-country sparrow.

Says_Phoebe.Description: Medium flycatcher with washed-out brown back, pale gray-brown breast, and peach-orange belly.
Says_Phoebe.Behavior: Wags tail constantly. Nests on cliff ledges, buildings, and under bridges.
Says_Phoebe.Habitat: Open and dry habitats including deserts, ranches, and cliff faces in western North America.
Says_Phoebe.Similar Looking Birds: Eastern Phoebe has white belly; Black Phoebe has black head; Say's Phoebe has orange belly.
Says_Phoebe.Best Ways to Identify: Peach-orange belly, washed-out brown back, and tail-wagging in dry western habitats.

Scaled_Quail.Description: Blue-gray quail with scaly pattern on breast and belly, white-tipped crest, and rusty flanks.
Scaled_Quail.Behavior: Prefers running over flying. Found in large coveys in dry desert grassland.
Scaled_Quail.Habitat: Desert grasslands and dry brushlands of the southwestern United States.
Scaled_Quail.Similar Looking Birds: Gambel's Quail has teardrop plume and chestnut flanks; Scaled has cotton-ball crest.
Scaled_Quail.Best Ways to Identify: Scaly breast pattern, white-tipped cotton-ball crest, and desert grassland habitat.

Scaly-breasted_Munia.Description:
Small finch, rich brown above, white below with
bold brown scalloping on breast
and flanks. About 4.5 inches.
Scaly-breasted_Munia.Behavior:
Highly gregarious, large flocks in open areas. Forages
for grass seeds. Common
invasive in Hawaii.
Scaly-breasted_Munia.Habitat:
Grasslands, roadsides, and open areas. Very common
introduced species throughout
Hawaiian Islands.
Scaly-breasted_Munia.Similar Looking Birds:
Chestnut Munia has chestnut head. Tricolored Munia
darker with black belly.
Scaly breast pattern distinctive.
Scaly-breasted_Munia.Best Ways to Identify:
Brown scaly pattern on white breast and flanks.
Brown above. Very common
in Hawaiian grasslands.

Scaly-naped_Pigeon.Description:
Large dark pigeon. Dark gray-brown overall with
iridescent reddish-purple on head and neck,
scaly pattern on hindneck. Red eye ring. About 15 inches.
Scaly-naped_Pigeon.Habitat:
Humid forest and wooded areas in Caribbean islands,
particularly Puerto Rico and Lesser Antilles.
Rare in Florida.
Scaly-naped_Pigeon.Similar Looking Birds:
White-crowned Pigeon more common in US range.
Scaly-naped darker with purple head gloss.
Scaly-naped_Pigeon.Best Ways to Identify:
Large dark pigeon with reddish-purple head gloss
and scaly hindneck pattern.
Found in Caribbean forests.

Scarlet_Ibis.Description:
Brilliant scarlet-red wading bird, same shape as White
Ibis. Red bill, legs, and plumage.
About 25 inches.
Scarlet_Ibis.Behavior:
Forages in tropical wetlands. Hybridizes with White
Ibis. Very rare vagrant to southern
Florida and Gulf Coast.
Scarlet_Ibis.Habitat:
Tropical South America and Caribbean. Very rare vagrant
to southern Florida and Gulf
Coast; some escapes.
Scarlet_Ibis.Similar Looking Birds:
White Ibis closely related and hybridizes. Scarlet
Ibis brilliantly red with no white.
Scarlet_Ibis.Best Ways to Identify:
Brilliant all-scarlet plumage unmistakable. Ibis shape
with downturned bill. Very rare
Florida vagrant or escape.

Scarlet_Tanager.Description:
Medium tanager. Male brilliant scarlet with jet black
wings. Female olive-green.
About 7 inches.
Scarlet_Tanager.Behavior:
Forages in deciduous forest canopy. One of most
striking North American birds.
Eastern forest breeder.
Scarlet_Tanager.Habitat:
Mature deciduous and mixed forests of eastern United
States. Winters in South America.
Scarlet_Tanager.Similar Looking Birds:
Summer Tanager male all red without black wings.
Western Tanager male has black
back with yellow head.
Scarlet_Tanager.Best Ways to Identify:
Male brilliant scarlet with jet black wings unique.
Female olive-green with dark
wing. Eastern deciduous forest.

Scissor-tailed_Flycatcher.Description: Pale gray flycatcher with salmon-pink sides and axillaries, and enormously long forked tail on adult.
Scissor-tailed_Flycatcher.Behavior: Catches insects in graceful aerial sorties. Very long tail used in courtship displays.
Scissor-tailed_Flycatcher.Habitat: Open grasslands and ranchlands of the south-central United States.
Scissor-tailed_Flycatcher.Similar Looking Birds: Fork-tailed Flycatcher is rarer vagrant; Scissor-tailed's pink sides and range are distinctive.
Scissor-tailed_Flycatcher.Best Ways to Identify: Extremely long scissor-like forked tail and salmon-pink sides -- unmistakable.

Scopolis_Shearwater.Description:
Large shearwater, brown above, white below, yellow
bill, pinkish legs. Very similar to
Cory's Shearwater. About 20 inches.
Scopolis_Shearwater.Behavior:
Mediterranean breeding shearwater that migrates into
North Atlantic. Rare but regular
off Atlantic coast.
Scopolis_Shearwater.Habitat:
North Atlantic Ocean. Rare but increasing vagrant
off Atlantic coast of North America.
Mediterranean breeder.
Scopolis_Shearwater.Similar Looking Birds:
Cory's Shearwater almost identical. Scopoli's has
smaller dark mark on outer primaries.
Scopolis_Shearwater.Best Ways to Identify:
Nearly identical to Cory's Shearwater. Less dark on
outer primaries from below.
Mediterranean counterpart to Cory's.

Scotts_Oriole.Description: Male has jet-black head, back, and breast with bright lemon-yellow body and wings with white bars.
Scotts_Oriole.Behavior: Nests in yucca plants. Sings rich warbling song from prominent perches.
Scotts_Oriole.Habitat: Desert mountain slopes with yuccas and pinyon-juniper in the southwestern United States.
Scotts_Oriole.Similar Looking Birds: Hooded Oriole male is orange with black back; Scott's male is yellow with black head.
Scotts_Oriole.Best Ways to Identify: Jet-black head and breast with lemon-yellow body -- nests in yucca in the desert southwest.

Scrippss_Murrelet.Description:
Small alcid. Black above, white below. White extends
up onto face, partial white eye ring. Short bill.
About 10 inches.
Scrippss_Murrelet.Behavior:
Nests in rock crevices on offshore California islands.
Chicks jump from nest cliff night of hatching.
Swims and dives for fish.
Scrippss_Murrelet.Habitat:
Nests on offshore islands of Southern California and
Baja. Forages in nearshore Pacific waters.
Scrippss_Murrelet.Similar Looking Birds:
Guadalupe Murrelet is sister species. Scripps's has
more white on face.
Scrippss_Murrelet.Best Ways to Identify:
Black and white alcid of Southern California waters.
White face pattern extends above and
around eye more than Guadalupe.

Seaside_Sparrow.Description: Dark streaked sparrow with yellow lore spot, short rounded tail, flat head, and heavy bill adapted for salt marsh.
Seaside_Sparrow.Behavior: Sings buzzy insect-like song from marsh vegetation; forages on mud for invertebrates; rarely leaves salt marsh.
Seaside_Sparrow.Habitat: Salt marshes along Atlantic and Gulf coasts; highly resident and tied to specific marsh grass communities.
Seaside_Sparrow.Similar Looking Birds: Nelson's Sparrow has orange wash on face; Saltmarsh Sparrow has sharper streaking and more orange tones.
Seaside_Sparrow.Best Ways to Identify: Yellow lore spot; olive-gray streaked plumage; flat head; salt marsh habitat; dark malar stripe; short tail.

Sedge_Warbler.Description:
Small warbler, streaked brown above with pale supercilium,
buff below. Rusty rump.
About 5 inches.
Sedge_Warbler.Behavior:
Sings from dense vegetation, often at night. Very
rare vagrant to eastern North
America from Europe.
Sedge_Warbler.Habitat:
Wetland edges, reed beds, and scrub near water
in Europe and Asia. Very rare
vagrant to North America.
Sedge_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds:
Marsh Wren also streaked but has barred back.
Sedge Wren smaller with
finely streaked crown.
Sedge_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify:
Streaked brown back, bold pale supercilium, rusty
rump. Rare European vagrant.
Associated with wetland vegetation.

Sedge_Wren.Description:
Small wren, streaked brown above with finely streaked
crown, buff below, barred wings.
About 4.5 inches.
Sedge_Wren.Behavior:
Secretive, creeps through wet meadows. Nomadic,
may breed in different locations
year to year. Hard to observe.
Sedge_Wren.Habitat:
Wet meadows, sedge marshes, and damp grassy areas
across eastern and central North
America.
Sedge_Wren.Similar Looking Birds:
Marsh Wren has bold white supercilium and plain
crown. Sedge lacks the
bold eyebrow.
Sedge_Wren.Best Ways to Identify:
Streaked crown (Marsh Wren has plain crown). Subtle
streaking throughout. Wet meadow
habitat, not cattails.

Semipalmated_Plover.Description: Small brown plover with single black breast band, orange-yellow legs, and small orange-based bill.
Semipalmated_Plover.Behavior: Very common migrant on mudflats and beaches. Runs and pauses like other plovers.
Semipalmated_Plover.Habitat: Mudflats, beaches, and coastal areas during migration across North America.
Semipalmated_Plover.Similar Looking Birds: Piping Plover is much paler; Killdeer has two breast bands; Semipalmated has one band.
Semipalmated_Plover.Best Ways to Identify: Brown back, single black breast band, and orange-yellow legs -- very common migrant.

Semipalmated_Sandpiper.Description: Small sandpiper with black legs, stubby straight bill, and gray-brown back with scaly pattern.
Semipalmated_Sandpiper.Behavior: One of the most numerous sandpipers in migration. Forms enormous flocks.
Semipalmated_Sandpiper.Habitat: Mudflats and beaches during migration across North America.
Semipalmated_Sandpiper.Similar Looking Birds: Least Sandpiper has yellow legs; Western Sandpiper has longer drooping bill.
Semipalmated_Sandpiper.Best Ways to Identify: Black legs and stubby bill -- abundant in coastal mudflats during migration.

Sharp-shinned_Hawk.Description: Smallest accipiter with short rounded wings, long squared tail, and orange-barred underparts.
Sharp-shinned_Hawk.Behavior: Pursues small birds through dense forest. Common at hawk watch sites in fall.
Sharp-shinned_Hawk.Habitat: Forests and woodlands across North America; common at hawk migration sites.
Sharp-shinned_Hawk.Similar Looking Birds: Cooper's Hawk is larger with rounded tail tip; Sharp-shinned has squared tail.
Sharp-shinned_Hawk.Best Ways to Identify: Smallest accipiter with squared tail -- compared to Cooper's Hawk which has rounded tail.

Sharp-tailed_Grouse.Description: Brown and white spotted grouse with short pointed tail; purple air sacs on neck; white underwing visible in flight.
Sharp-tailed_Grouse.Behavior: Males dance on leks doing rapid foot stomping and cooing displays; flocks in winter; forages for berries and buds.
Sharp-tailed_Grouse.Habitat: Prairie grasslands, agricultural fields, and forest-grassland edges of northern Great Plains and Canada.
Sharp-tailed_Grouse.Similar Looking Birds: Prairie-chickens have rounded tails and horizontal barring; Ruffed Grouse has fan-shaped tail and forest habitat.
Sharp-tailed_Grouse.Best Ways to Identify: Pointed white-edged tail; spotted not barred underparts; purple neck sacs in display; prairie and parkland habitat.

Sharp-tailed_Sandpiper.Description:
Medium sandpiper. Bright rufous cap, streaked breast
fading to spotted flanks, olive-brown back.
About 8.5 inches.
Sharp-tailed_Sandpiper.Behavior:
Forages in wet grassy areas and mudflats. Migrates
through western Alaska in fall; rare on Pacific
coast.
Sharp-tailed_Sandpiper.Habitat:
Breeds in Siberia. Migrates through western Alaska.
Winters in Australia. Regular migrant in
western Alaska; rare elsewhere on Pacific coast.
Sharp-tailed_Sandpiper.Similar Looking Birds:
Pectoral Sandpiper similar. Sharp-tailed has rufous
cap and spotted (not streaked) lower breast.
Sharp-tailed_Sandpiper.Best Ways to Identify:
Bright rufous cap, olive-brown back, and spotted
flanks. Regular fall migrant in
western Alaska.

Shiny_Cowbird.Description:
Medium cowbird. Male entirely glossy black with purple
iridescence. Female dull brown.
About 7.5 inches.
Shiny_Cowbird.Behavior:
Brood parasite like other cowbirds. Spreading northward
into Florida and southeastern
United States from Caribbean.
Shiny_Cowbird.Habitat:
Open fields, farmland, and brushy areas. Established
in Florida and Caribbean.
Native to South America.
Shiny_Cowbird.Similar Looking Birds:
Brown-headed Cowbird male has brown head. Rusty Blackbird
thinner bill. All-glossy
black male distinctive.
Shiny_Cowbird.Best Ways to Identify:
Male all glossy black with purple sheen. Female dull
brown. Brood parasite.
Expanding range in Florida.

Short-billed_Dowitcher.Description: Medium shorebird with long bill, rusty-and-white speckled breeding plumage, and white wedge on back.
Short-billed_Dowitcher.Behavior: Probes in sewing-machine fashion. Prefers saltwater habitats. Mellow tu-tu-tu call.
Short-billed_Dowitcher.Habitat: Coastal mudflats and beaches during migration; Arctic tundra for breeding.
Short-billed_Dowitcher.Similar Looking Birds: Long-billed Dowitcher prefers freshwater; Short-billed prefers coastal salt flats and gives soft call.
Short-billed_Dowitcher.Best Ways to Identify: Mellow tu-tu-tu call and preference for coastal salt flats versus Long-billed's preference for freshwater.

Short-billed_Gull.Description:
Medium gull, pale gray back, small stubby bill, large
dark eye. White body, yellow-green bill.
About 16 inches.
Short-billed_Gull.Behavior:
Pacific coast counterpart to Common Gull of Europe.
Forages on tidal flats and coastlines.
Common in Pacific Northwest winter.
Short-billed_Gull.Similar Looking Birds:
Ring-billed Gull similar but larger with thicker bill.
Short-billed has distinctly small stubby bill.
Short-billed_Gull.Best Ways to Identify:
Small stubby bill and large dark eye. Pacific coast
species. Pale gray back, white body.
Winters on coastal beaches and flats.

Short-eared_Owl.Description: Medium owl with buffy streaked plumage, yellow eyes, black eye patches, and tiny barely visible ear tufts.
Short-eared_Owl.Behavior: Hunts voles in low quartering flight at dawn and dusk; roosts on ground; wanders with prey availability.
Short-eared_Owl.Habitat: Open grasslands, marshes, tundra, and agricultural fields; nomadic following vole population cycles.
Short-eared_Owl.Similar Looking Birds: Long-eared Owl has prominent ear tufts and orange facial disc; Northern Harrier has similar buoyant flight.
Short-eared_Owl.Best Ways to Identify: Yellow eyes with black mascara marks; buoyant floppy flight low over fields; daytime hunting; open country.

Short-tailed_Albatross.Description:
Large albatross, white body and head with golden-buff
wash, pink bill, dark wings with white
shoulder patches. About 36 inches.
Short-tailed_Albatross.Behavior:
Critically endangered; recovering from near extinction.
Breeds on Torishima Island, Japan.
Regular rare sighting in North Pacific.
Short-tailed_Albatross.Habitat:
North Pacific Ocean. Rare but regular off Alaska and
Pacific coast. Recovering endangered
species from Japan.
Short-tailed_Albatross.Similar Looking Birds:
Laysan Albatross lacks golden head wash. Short-tailed's
large pink bill diagnostic.
Short-tailed_Albatross.Best Ways to Identify:
Golden-buff head wash and large pink bill. White
back with dark wings. Endangered
species recovering in North Pacific.

Short-tailed_Hawk.Description:
Small buteo, two morphs: light morph white below
and dark morph all dark. Clean white
underparts in light morph. About 15 inches.
Short-tailed_Hawk.Habitat:
Dense hammock and cypress swamp forest in southern
Florida. Rare in Texas and
Arizona.
Short-tailed_Hawk.Similar Looking Birds:
Broad-winged Hawk similar light morph. Short-tailed's
very clean white underparts distinctive.
Short-tailed_Hawk.Best Ways to Identify:
Light morph: brilliant clean white below. Dark morph:
all dark. Both show clean two-toned
pattern. Florida specialist.

Short-tailed_Shearwater.Description:
Medium dark shearwater, dark brown overall with pale
underwing and short stubby bill.
About 16 inches.
Short-tailed_Shearwater.Behavior:
Breeds in Australia; migrates north through Pacific
to Bering Sea. Abundant in North
Pacific; common off Pacific coast.
Short-tailed_Shearwater.Habitat:
North Pacific Ocean. Common offshore Pacific coast
particularly in winter. Migrates from
Australian breeding grounds.
Short-tailed_Shearwater.Similar Looking Birds:
Sooty Shearwater similar but has more silvery underwing.
Short-tailed has shorter bill.
Short-tailed_Shearwater.Best Ways to Identify:
Dark shearwater with short stubby bill. Pale grayish
underwing. Very common in North
Pacific winter, abundant off Alaska.

Siberian_Accentor.Description:
Small sparrow-like bird, streaked brown above, orange-buff
below with white throat,
bold dark facial pattern. About 5.5 inches.
Siberian_Accentor.Behavior:
Forages on ground in dense scrub. Rare vagrant to
western Alaska and occasionally
farther inland from Siberia.
Siberian_Accentor.Habitat:
Mountain scrub and taiga of Siberia. Rare vagrant
to western Alaska and
Aleutian Islands.
Siberian_Accentor.Similar Looking Birds:
House Sparrow lacks orange-buff underparts and bold
face. No similar accentor
in North America.
Siberian_Accentor.Best Ways to Identify:
Orange-buff underparts with dark facial pattern. White
throat. Rare Alaska vagrant
from Siberia.

Siberian_Blue_Robin.Description:
Small chat-flycatcher. Male brilliant blue above,
white below with blue side band.
Female brown above. About 5.5 inches.
Siberian_Blue_Robin.Behavior:
Skulks in dense undergrowth near ground. Rare vagrant
to western Alaska from
Siberia.
Siberian_Blue_Robin.Habitat:
Dense forest undergrowth of Siberia and East Asia.
Rare vagrant to western Alaska
and Aleutian Islands.
Siberian_Blue_Robin.Similar Looking Birds:
Indigo Bunting smaller and different shape. No other
bright blue robin in Alaska.
Siberian_Blue_Robin.Best Ways to Identify:
Male brilliant blue above with white underparts.
Blue band on sides. Rare
Alaska vagrant from Siberia.

Siberian_House-Martin.Description:
Small swallow, blue-black above, white rump, white
underparts. Slightly forked tail.
About 5 inches.
Siberian_House-Martin.Behavior:
Colonial nester on cliffs. Forages over open areas.
Rare vagrant to western Alaska
and Aleutian Islands.
Siberian_House-Martin.Habitat:
Open areas, cliffs, and river valleys in Siberia
and northeastern Asia. Rare vagrant
to western Alaska.
Siberian_House-Martin.Similar Looking Birds:
Common House-Martin very similar but different range.
Cliff Swallow has rusty
rump. Tree Swallow has green back.
Siberian_House-Martin.Best Ways to Identify:
White rump, blue-black above, white below. Tiny
swallow. Alaska vagrant from
Siberia. Slightly forked tail.

Siberian_Pipit.Description:
Small pipit, olive-brown streaked above, buff-white
below with dark streaking. Very
similar to American Pipit. About 6 inches.
Siberian_Pipit.Behavior:
Forages on ground in open areas. Rare vagrant to
western Alaska from Siberia.
Recently separated from American Pipit.
Siberian_Pipit.Habitat:
Open areas, tundra, and meadows in Siberia. Rare
vagrant to western Alaska.
Siberian_Pipit.Similar Looking Birds:
American Pipit nearly identical; best separated by
subtle plumage and call differences.
Range overlap in Alaska.
Siberian_Pipit.Best Ways to Identify:
Very similar to American Pipit. Subtle differences
in streaking and buff tones.
Western Alaska vagrant from Siberia.

Siberian_Rubythroat.Description:
Small chat. Male has brilliant red throat bordered
by white, brown above, white
below. About 5.5 inches.
Siberian_Rubythroat.Behavior:
Skulks in dense thickets. Rich melodious song. Rare
vagrant to western Alaska and
Aleutian Islands from Asia.
Siberian_Rubythroat.Habitat:
Dense scrub, forest edge undergrowth in Siberia.
Rare vagrant to western Alaska
and Aleutians.
Siberian_Rubythroat.Similar Looking Birds:
Bluethroat has blue throat, breeds in Alaska.
No other red-throated small bird
in Alaska habitat.
Siberian_Rubythroat.Best Ways to Identify:
Brilliant red throat on male distinctive. Brown above,
white below. Rare Alaska
vagrant from Siberia.

Siberian_Sand-Plover.Description:
Medium plover. Breeding adult has rufous-orange breast
band, gray-brown back, black mask. Non-breeding
plain gray-brown. About 8 inches.
Siberian_Sand-Plover.Behavior:
Forages on sandy beaches and mudflats for invertebrates.
Rare vagrant to Pacific coast from Asian
breeding grounds.
Siberian_Sand-Plover.Habitat:
Breeds on central Asian mountains and Siberian tundra.
Winters on Asian and African coasts.
Rare vagrant to Pacific coast of North America.
Siberian_Sand-Plover.Similar Looking Birds:
Greater Sand-Plover larger with heavier bill. Recently
split; formerly called Mongolian Plover.
Siberian_Sand-Plover.Best Ways to Identify:
Rufous breast band in breeding plumage. Smaller
and slimmer bill than Greater Sand-Plover.
Rare vagrant on Pacific coast.

Siberian_Stonechat.Description:
Small chat. Male black head and back, white neck
patch, orange-rufous breast. Female
brown. About 5 inches.
Siberian_Stonechat.Behavior:
Perches upright on low vegetation, bobs tail. Rare
vagrant to western Alaska and
Aleutian Islands from Siberia.
Siberian_Stonechat.Habitat:
Open country with scattered scrub in Siberia and
Asia. Rare vagrant to western
Alaska.
Siberian_Stonechat.Similar Looking Birds:
European Stonechat very similar. American Robin much
larger with red breast. No
similar chat in range.
Siberian_Stonechat.Best Ways to Identify:
Male black head with white neck patch and orange
breast. Upright perching posture.
Rare Alaska vagrant.

Silver_Pheasant.Description:
Large pheasant. Male white above with fine black
markings, blue-black below, red
facial skin. About 40 inches.
Silver_Pheasant.Behavior:
Forages on ground in dense forest. Shy and secretive.
Small introduced populations
in North America.
Silver_Pheasant.Habitat:
Dense forest and woodland. Small introduced populations
in parts of North America.
Native to Southeast Asia.
Silver_Pheasant.Similar Looking Birds:
Ring-necked Pheasant male different coloration. No
other large pheasant with white
back in range.
Silver_Pheasant.Best Ways to Identify:
Male white above with black markings and blue-black
below. Introduced populations.
Red facial skin distinctive.

Sinaloa_Wren.Description:
Medium wren, rusty-brown above with barred wings
and tail, white supercilium,
streaked head. About 5.5 inches.
Sinaloa_Wren.Behavior:
Skulks in dense thorn scrub. Loud rich song.
Very rare vagrant to southeastern
Arizona from Mexico.
Sinaloa_Wren.Habitat:
Dense thorn scrub of western Mexico. Very rare
vagrant to extreme southeastern Arizona.
Sinaloa_Wren.Similar Looking Birds:
Bewick's Wren larger with longer tail and different
habitat. Canyon Wren has white
throat and different habitat.
Sinaloa_Wren.Best Ways to Identify:
Rusty-brown wren with bold white supercilium in
Arizona thorn scrub. Very rare.
Loud melodious song.

Slate-throated_Redstart.Description:
Medium warbler, slate-gray above, bright red breast,
white outer tail feathers fanned.
About 5.5 inches.
Slate-throated_Redstart.Behavior:
Fans and droops wings and tail to flush insects.
Rare vagrant to Arizona and
New Mexico from Mexico.
Slate-throated_Redstart.Habitat:
Pine-oak mountain forests of Mexico and Central America.
Rare vagrant to Arizona
and New Mexico.
Slate-throated_Redstart.Similar Looking Birds:
Painted Redstart has white wing patch. American Redstart
different pattern. Red breast
distinctive.
Slate-throated_Redstart.Best Ways to Identify:
Slate-gray with red breast, white outer tail feathers.
Fan display behavior. Rare
Arizona vagrant from Mexico.

Slaty-backed_Gull.Description:
Large gull, very dark slate-gray back, pink legs,
broad white tertial crescent. "String-of-pearls"
wingtip pattern. About 25 inches.
Slaty-backed_Gull.Behavior:
Breeds in Siberia; winters in Asia. Rare but regular
visitor to western Alaska; occasional
vagrant to Pacific coast.
Slaty-backed_Gull.Habitat:
Rocky Siberian coastlines. Rare visitor to western
Alaska and Aleutian Islands; occasional
on Pacific coast.
Slaty-backed_Gull.Similar Looking Birds:
Western Gull similar but paler gray back. Slaty-backed's
very dark back and pink legs distinctive.
Slaty-backed_Gull.Best Ways to Identify:
Very dark slate back with pink legs. Broad white
tertial crescent, "string-of-pearls" wingtip.
Asian species rare on Pacific coast.

Slender-billed_Curlew.Description:
Medium curlew, possibly extinct. Brown streaked plumage
with distinctive round dark spots on flanks,
slender bill. About 16 inches.
Slender-billed_Curlew.Behavior:
Formerly wintered in Mediterranean; now possibly extinct.
Last confirmed sighting 1995. Listed as critically
endangered or extinct.
Slender-billed_Curlew.Habitat:
Bred in western Siberia. Wintered in Mediterranean
wetlands. Possibly extinct; no confirmed
sightings since 1990s.
Slender-billed_Curlew.Similar Looking Birds:
Eurasian Curlew similar but lacks round flank spots.
Slender-billed's spots diagnostic.
Slender-billed_Curlew.Best Ways to Identify:
Round dark spots on flanks diagnostic if seen.
Possibly extinct since the 1990s.
Extremely rare or extinct.

Small-billed_Elaenia.Description:
Small flycatcher, olive above, pale below, two wing
bars, small bill. Hidden white crown
patch. About 5 inches.
Small-billed_Elaenia.Behavior:
Migrant; breeds in South America, winters in tropics.
Very rare vagrant to North American
Atlantic coast.
Small-billed_Elaenia.Habitat:
South American woodlands. Very rare vagrant to Atlantic
coast of North America.
Small-billed_Elaenia.Similar Looking Birds:
Other elaenias very similar. Small bill and plain
olive plumage.
Small-billed_Elaenia.Best Ways to Identify:
Small olive flycatcher with small bill, two wing bars.
Very rare Atlantic vagrant from
South America.

Smew.Description:
Small merganser. Male is striking white with black
eye patch, back, and wing marks. Female gray-brown
with chestnut cap and white cheeks. About 16 inches.
Smew.Behavior:
Dives for fish and aquatic invertebrates. Nests
in tree cavities. Rare vagrant to North
America from Eurasia.
Smew.Habitat:
Breeds in northern Eurasian boreal forests near
lakes and rivers. Winters on European lakes.
Rare vagrant to North American Atlantic coast.
Smew.Similar Looking Birds:
Bufflehead has similar small size. Male Smew's
white plumage unique among North American ducks.
Smew.Best Ways to Identify:
Male's nearly all-white plumage with black eye patch
and back distinctive. Female's rufous
cap and white face pattern.

Smiths_Longspur.Description:
Medium bunting-like bird, streaked brown above, rich
buff-orange below with black-and-white
face pattern on male. About 6 inches.
Smiths_Longspur.Behavior:
Walks on ground in flocks. Polyandrous breeding system.
Winters in specific grass
fields, often hard to find.
Smiths_Longspur.Habitat:
Breeds on tundra, winters in short-grass fields
of Great Plains from Oklahoma
to Tennessee.
Smiths_Longspur.Similar Looking Birds:
Lapland Longspur male has rusty nape. Chestnut-collared
Longspur has chestnut collar.
Smiths_Longspur.Best Ways to Identify:
Rich buff-orange underparts, male has black-and-white
face. Specific winter grass
fields. Secretive ground bird.

Smooth-billed_Ani.Description:
All-black cuckoo family bird with long floppy tail
and large laterally compressed bill with curved
ridge on top. About 14 inches.
Smooth-billed_Ani.Behavior:
Lives in social groups; multiple pairs share nest.
Follows cattle to catch disturbed insects. Found in
southern Florida; declining in US range.
Smooth-billed_Ani.Habitat:
Open brushy areas, fields, and scrubby vegetation
in Florida, Caribbean, and South America. Found
near livestock in tropical lowlands.
Smooth-billed_Ani.Similar Looking Birds:
Groove-billed Ani very similar but smaller with
grooved bill. Grackles lack compressed bill.
Smooth-billed_Ani.Best Ways to Identify:
All-black with enormous smooth-ridged bill unique
among Florida birds. Long floppy tail and
clumsy flight distinctive.

Snail_Kite.Description: Medium raptor; male slate gray with red eyes and orange cere; female brown streaked; strongly hooked bill.
Snail_Kite.Behavior: Snatches apple snails from water surface; soars over marshes; endangered in Florida; highly social nester.
Snail_Kite.Habitat: Freshwater marshes and lakes in Florida, especially Lake Okeechobee and associated wetlands.
Snail_Kite.Similar Looking Birds: Northern Harrier has owl-like face and longer tail; Hook-billed Kite in tropics has very different plumage.
Snail_Kite.Best Ways to Identify: Extremely hooked narrow bill; white base of tail; red eye and orange cere; slow buoyant flight over marshes.

Snow_Bunting.Description: Breeding male mostly white with black back and wingtips; winter birds buffy with white wings contrasting in flight.
Snow_Bunting.Behavior: Flocks wheel in flight showing white wing flashes; forages on ground for seeds; breeds on Arctic tundra.
Snow_Bunting.Habitat: Arctic tundra for breeding; winters in open fields, beaches, and coastal dunes of northern US and Canada.
Snow_Bunting.Similar Looking Birds: McKay's Bunting is nearly all white with less black; Lapland Longspur shows less white in wings in flight.
Snow_Bunting.Best Ways to Identify: Extensive white in wings visible in flight; whitish overall in winter; black and white breeding plumage; open fields.

Snow_Goose.Description: White goose with black wingtips and pink bill with dark grinning patch; blue morph has dark body and white head.
Snow_Goose.Behavior: Migrates in enormous flocks; forages in agricultural fields; overabundant and damaging Arctic tundra habitat.
Snow_Goose.Habitat: Breeds on Arctic tundra; winters in coastal marshes, rice fields, and agricultural areas across southern US.
Snow_Goose.Similar Looking Birds: Ross's Goose is smaller with stubbier bill and no grinning patch; Cackling Goose is very different darker species.
Snow_Goose.Best Ways to Identify: White body with black wingtips; pink bill with black grinning patch; large flocks; blue morph also common.

Snowy_Egret.Description: Small all-white egret with black bill, black legs, and bright yellow feet; breeding adults have wispy plumes.
Snowy_Egret.Behavior: Actively forages by shuffling yellow feet to stir prey; more animated than Great Egret; colonial nester.
Snowy_Egret.Habitat: Freshwater and saltwater marshes, mudflats, ponds, and coastal lagoons throughout Americas.
Snowy_Egret.Similar Looking Birds: Great Egret is much larger with yellow bill; Cattle Egret is shorter with yellow bill and buff breeding plumes.
Snowy_Egret.Best Ways to Identify: Yellow feet contrasting with black legs; black bill; small size; wispy breeding plumes; active foraging style.

Snowy_Owl.Description: Large white owl; adult male nearly pure white; females and young have dark barring; yellow eyes; no ear tufts.
Snowy_Owl.Behavior: Hunts lemmings on tundra; irrupts south in winter during low prey years; perches prominently on ground or posts.
Snowy_Owl.Habitat: Open Arctic tundra for breeding; open country, airports, and beaches during southern winter irruptions.
Snowy_Owl.Similar Looking Birds: Barn Owl is smaller with heart-shaped face; Short-eared Owl is buffy brown; no other large white owl exists.
Snowy_Owl.Best Ways to Identify: Large white owl; yellow eyes; diurnal activity; perches on ground or fence posts; open treeless landscapes.

Snowy_Plover.Description: Small pale sandy-colored plover with dark partial breast band, dark ear patch, and thin dark bill; slender build.
Snowy_Plover.Behavior: Runs quickly on beaches; nests in open sand scrapes; chick precocial; threatened by beach disturbance.
Snowy_Plover.Habitat: Sandy beaches, alkali flats, and dry lakeshores of western US and Gulf Coast; year-round on coastal beaches.
Snowy_Plover.Similar Looking Birds: Piping Plover has orange bill base and complete or thicker breast band; Wilson's Plover has thicker bill.
Snowy_Plover.Best Ways to Identify: Pale sandy plumage; incomplete dark breast patches on sides; thin dark bill; dark ear patch; slim proportions.

Social_Flycatcher.Description:
Small flycatcher, olive-brown above, yellow below,
gray head with white supercilium and
hidden orange crown patch. About 7 inches.
Social_Flycatcher.Behavior:
Bold and aggressive; mobs much larger birds. Common
resident from Mexico south. Very rare
vagrant to southern Texas.
Social_Flycatcher.Habitat:
Forest edge and open areas from Mexico to South America.
Very rare vagrant to
southern Texas.
Social_Flycatcher.Similar Looking Birds:
Kiskadee and other tyrannids similar. Social Flycatcher
smaller with gray head.
Social_Flycatcher.Best Ways to Identify:
Gray head with white supercilium, yellow below. Small
and bold. Very rare vagrant from
Mexico to Texas.

Solitary_Sandpiper.Description: Medium sandpiper with dark olive-brown back heavily spotted white, white eye-ring, and boldly barred tail.
Solitary_Sandpiper.Behavior: Usually alone as name suggests; bobs body when foraging; nests in old songbird nests in boreal trees.
Solitary_Sandpiper.Habitat: Boreal forest ponds for nesting; freshwater pools, streams, and flooded fields during migration.
Solitary_Sandpiper.Similar Looking Birds: Spotted Sandpiper teeters continuously; Lesser Yellowlegs has yellow legs and longer bill; Green Sandpiper similar.
Solitary_Sandpiper.Best Ways to Identify: Boldly barred white outer tail; white eye-ring; spotted back; dark legs; bobs body; solitary freshwater habitat.

Solitary_Snipe.Description:
Large snipe. Pale grayish-brown streaked plumage
with rufous tones, long bill, rather pale and
washed out appearance. About 12 inches.
Solitary_Snipe.Behavior:
Solitary; rarely flushes. Forages along mountain
streams in Asia. Very rare vagrant to
western Alaska from Siberia.
Solitary_Snipe.Habitat:
Mountain streams and wet rocky areas in Asia.
Winters in South and East Asia. Very rare
vagrant to western Alaska.
Solitary_Snipe.Similar Looking Birds:
Common Snipe similar. Solitary Snipe larger and
paler with rufous tones.
Solitary_Snipe.Best Ways to Identify:
Large, pale snipe. Rufous tones. Found along
mountain streams. Very rare vagrant
in western Alaska.

Song_Sparrow.Description: Medium brown sparrow with heavy brown streaks converging in large central breast spot; long rounded tail; gray face.
Song_Sparrow.Behavior: Sings complex melodious songs from exposed perches; pumps tail in flight; common backyard species.
Song_Sparrow.Habitat: Thickets, gardens, marsh edges, and shrubby areas across most of North America; highly variable subspecies.
Song_Sparrow.Similar Looking Birds: Lincoln's Sparrow is buffier with finer streaking; Savannah Sparrow has notched tail and yellow lore.
Song_Sparrow.Best Ways to Identify: Large central breast spot; heavy streaking; long rounded tail pumped in flight; variable but streaked throughout.

Song_Thrush.Description:
Medium thrush, warm brown above, white to buff
below with bold dark arrowhead
spots. About 9 inches.
Song_Thrush.Behavior:
Famous for smashing snail shells against stones.
Repeats song phrases two or
three times. Rare vagrant to North America.
Song_Thrush.Habitat:
Woodland, gardens, hedgerows across Europe. Rare
vagrant to eastern and western
coasts of North America.
Song_Thrush.Similar Looking Birds:
Mistle Thrush larger with gray-brown tones. Redwing
has red flank patch.
American Robin has red-orange breast.
Song_Thrush.Best Ways to Identify:
Dark arrowhead spots on pale buff breast. Warm
brown upperparts. Rare
European vagrant. Song repetitions distinctive.

Sooty_Grouse.Description:
Large forest grouse. Male sooty gray-brown with
yellow-orange eye combs and bare yellow-orange neck
sacs. Female cryptically mottled brown. About 20 inches.
Sooty_Grouse.Behavior:
Males hoot from treetops in spring. Moves upslope
in winter to feed on conifer needles. More
arboreal than other North American grouse.
Sooty_Grouse.Habitat:
Pacific coast coniferous forests from Alaska to
California. Prefers dense fir and hemlock
forests on mountain slopes.
Sooty_Grouse.Similar Looking Birds:
Dusky Grouse nearly identical; separated by range
(west of Rockies vs. east).
Sooty_Grouse.Best Ways to Identify:
Male's yellow-orange neck sacs and eye combs.
Sooty gray-brown plumage. Found in
Pacific coast conifer forests.

Sooty_Shearwater.Description: All dark brown shearwater with pale silvery-white wing linings contrasting with dark upperwing; long pointed wings.
Sooty_Shearwater.Behavior: Migrates in enormous flocks offshore; stiff-winged gliding flight; dives for fish and squid; transoceanic migrant.
Sooty_Shearwater.Habitat: Open ocean; one of most abundant seabirds; breeds in Southern Hemisphere; visits North Pacific and Atlantic coasts.
Sooty_Shearwater.Similar Looking Birds: Short-tailed Shearwater is very similar but has steeper forehead; dark-phase shearwaters lack white wing linings.
Sooty_Shearwater.Best Ways to Identify: Dark brown body; pale silvery underwing linings; long narrow wings; stiff shearwearing flight over open ocean.

Sooty_Tern.Description: Medium tern with jet black upperparts, white forehead and underparts, deeply forked tail, and black bill.
Sooty_Tern.Behavior: Colonial breeder on tropical islands; rarely lands on water; snatches fish from surface; raucous calls.
Sooty_Tern.Habitat: Tropical and subtropical oceans worldwide; breeds on coral islands including Dry Tortugas in Florida.
Sooty_Tern.Similar Looking Birds: Bridled Tern has white collar and browner back; Aleutian Tern has gray underparts; different geographic ranges.
Sooty_Tern.Best Ways to Identify: Black back contrasting with white forehead and underparts; long forked tail; tropical ocean habitat; wide white forehead.

Sora.Description: Small plump rail with yellow bill, black face mask, gray breast, and brown barred flanks; short upturned tail.
Sora.Behavior: Gives descending whinny call; secretive in marsh vegetation; flushes reluctantly; very common but rarely seen.
Sora.Habitat: Freshwater marshes with cattails and sedges throughout North America; migrates to Central America in winter.
Sora.Similar Looking Birds: Virginia Rail is larger with long reddish bill; Yellow Rail is smaller and very secretive with white wing patches.
Sora.Best Ways to Identify: Yellow bill; black face patch; gray underparts with barred flanks; short tail cocked up; freshwater marsh calls.

South_Polar_Skua.Description:
Large powerful seabird. Variable plumage from all-
dark brown to pale-headed form. White wing flash,
broad wings. About 21 inches.
South_Polar_Skua.Habitat:
Breeds in Antarctic. Pelagic migrant to northern
oceans in austral winter. Seen offshore
both coasts of North America.
South_Polar_Skua.Similar Looking Birds:
Great Skua very similar. South Polar Skua has
pale morph; browner Great Skua.
South_Polar_Skua.Best Ways to Identify:
Pale-headed morph distinctive. Dark morph nearly
identical to Great Skua. White wing
flash in flight.

Southern_Lapwing.Description:
Large plover with black breast, gray-brown back,
pinkish-red facial skin, backward-pointing head crest,
carpal spurs. About 14 inches.
Southern_Lapwing.Behavior:
Loud, aggressive defender of territory. Common
in South American grasslands. Rare vagrant to
Caribbean and southern US from South America.
Southern_Lapwing.Habitat:
Open grasslands, wetland edges, and agricultural
areas in South America. Rare vagrant to
Caribbean and southern Florida.
Southern_Lapwing.Similar Looking Birds:
Northern Lapwing similar in shape but different
coloring. No other lapwing in range.
Southern_Lapwing.Best Ways to Identify:
Black breast band, gray back, red facial skin,
and backward-pointing crest distinctive.
Loud persistent calling.

Southern_Martin.Description:
Large swallow. Male all glossy blue-black. Female
brown above, pale below with
streaked breast. About 7 inches.
Southern_Martin.Behavior:
Aerial forager over open country. Very rare vagrant
to North America from South
America.
Southern_Martin.Habitat:
Open country, cliffs, and buildings in South America.
Very rare vagrant to North
America.
Southern_Martin.Similar Looking Birds:
Purple Martin very similar; male indistinguishable
in field. Female Purple Martin
has less streaking below.
Southern_Martin.Best Ways to Identify:
Nearly identical to Purple Martin. Male all dark.
Female streaked. South American
species, very rare vagrant.

Spectacled_Eider.Description:
Large sea duck. Male has white body, black breast,
green head with bold white eye patches rimmed in black
creating a spectacle pattern. Female brown. About 21 inches.
Spectacled_Eider.Behavior:
Dives for bivalves, crustaceans, and marine
invertebrates. Nests on coastal tundra. Winters
in Bering Sea polynyas. Threatened species.
Spectacled_Eider.Habitat:
Breeds on coastal tundra of western Alaska and
Siberia. Winters in large sea ice openings
in the Bering Sea.
Spectacled_Eider.Similar Looking Birds:
Other eiders lack the spectacle face pattern.
Male unmistakable among North American sea ducks.
Spectacled_Eider.Best Ways to Identify:
Male's bold white eye patch rimmed in black and
green gives distinctive spectacled appearance.
Female has faint pale eye ring.

Spoon-billed_Sandpiper.Description:
Critically endangered tiny sandpiper with extraordinary
spatula-shaped bill tip. Reddish-brown breeding
plumage, white below. About 6 inches.
Spoon-billed_Sandpiper.Behavior:
Sweeps bill side to side in shallow water. Critically
endangered; fewer than 400 remain. Rare vagrant
to Pacific coast.
Spoon-billed_Sandpiper.Habitat:
Breeds on Chukotka Peninsula, Russia. Winters in
Southeast Asian mudflats. Extremely rare vagrant
to Pacific coast of North America.
Spoon-billed_Sandpiper.Similar Looking Birds:
Red-necked Stint similar size. Bill shape unmistakable
when seen.

Spot-breasted_Oriole.Description:
Large oriole, orange with black back and wings,
black spots on breast sides,
white wing bars. About 9.5 inches.
Spot-breasted_Oriole.Behavior:
Forages in flowering trees. Established introduced
population in southeastern Florida.
Beautiful loud song.
Spot-breasted_Oriole.Habitat:
Suburban areas, gardens, and open woodland. Introduced
to southeastern Florida.
Native to Central America.
Spot-breasted_Oriole.Similar Looking Birds:
Baltimore Oriole lacks spots on breast. Scott's Oriole
has black head. Spots
on breast distinctive.
Spot-breasted_Oriole.Best Ways to Identify:
Black spots on breast sides distinctive. Orange with
black back. Southeastern Florida
introduced population.

Spotted_Dove.Description:
Medium dove with pinkish-brown body, long tail,
and distinctive black hindneck collar with white
spots like a necklace. About 12 inches.
Spotted_Dove.Habitat:
Urban parks, gardens, agricultural areas, and open
woodland. Introduced populations in Los Angeles
area and Hawaiian Islands.
Spotted_Dove.Similar Looking Birds:
Eurasian Collared-Dove similar size but lacks spotted
neck collar. Mourning Dove slimmer.
Spotted_Dove.Best Ways to Identify:
Black and white spotted collar on hindneck unique
among North American doves. Brown-pink plumage
and long rounded tail.

Spotted_Flycatcher.Description:
Small flycatcher, gray-brown above with streaked
crown, white below with streaked
breast. About 5.5 inches.
Spotted_Flycatcher.Behavior:
Sallies from upright perch returning to same spot.
Rare vagrant to North America
from Europe.
Spotted_Flycatcher.Habitat:
Open woodland and gardens in Europe and Asia.
Very rare vagrant to North America.
Spotted_Flycatcher.Similar Looking Birds:
Gray-streaked Flycatcher has gray-brown breast streaking
without crown streaking.
European vagrant context helpful.
Spotted_Flycatcher.Best Ways to Identify:
Streaked crown distinguishes from other Muscicapa flycatchers.
Streaked breast. Very rare
European vagrant to East Coast.

Spotted_Owl.Description: Medium owl with dark brown plumage and white spots covering breast and belly; dark eyes; no ear tufts; round head.
Spotted_Owl.Behavior: Nocturnal hunter of flying squirrels and woodrats; hooting calls; threatened by Barred Owl competition.
Spotted_Owl.Habitat: Old-growth and mature forests of Pacific Coast and Rocky Mountains; needs large trees and dense canopy.
Spotted_Owl.Similar Looking Birds: Barred Owl has streaked belly and barred breast; Barn Owl is paler with heart-shaped face; larger owls have ear tufts.
Spotted_Owl.Best Ways to Identify: Dark brown with white spots on belly; dark brown eyes; old-growth forest; no ear tufts; round facial disc.

Spotted_Rail.Description:
Medium rail. Dark brown with bold white spots on
breast and flanks, long red bill with green base,
red legs. About 10 inches.
Spotted_Rail.Behavior:
Secretive; skulks in dense marsh vegetation. Rarely
seen. Rare vagrant to US from Caribbean
and South America.
Spotted_Rail.Habitat:
Freshwater marshes and wet grasslands in Caribbean,
South America, and occasionally Mexico. Rare
vagrant to Gulf Coast states.
Spotted_Rail.Similar Looking Birds:
Sora and other small rails. Spotted Rail's bold
white spots and red bill distinctive.
Spotted_Rail.Best Ways to Identify:
Bold white spots on dark brown plumage with bright
red bill. Found in dense marsh
vegetation. Very secretive.

Spotted_Redshank.Description:
Large sandpiper. Breeding adult entirely sooty black
with white spots; non-breeding pale gray above,
white below. Long red legs. About 12 inches.
Spotted_Redshank.Behavior:
Forages by wading and swimming. Rare vagrant to
both coasts of North America from Eurasia.
Spotted_Redshank.Habitat:
Breeds on Eurasian subarctic tundra. Winters on
African and Asian coasts. Rare vagrant
to North America.
Spotted_Redshank.Similar Looking Birds:
Common Redshank has white wing patches. Breeding
Spotted Redshank all-black unmistakable.
Spotted_Redshank.Best Ways to Identify:
Breeding adult all-black with white spots unmistakable.
Non-breeding pale gray. Long red
legs and bill.

Spotted_Sandpiper.Description: Small sandpiper; breeding plumage has bold black spots on white underparts; orange bill; constantly teeters body.
Spotted_Sandpiper.Behavior: Teeters rear end up and down constantly while walking; low stiff-winged flight; polyandrous breeding system.
Spotted_Sandpiper.Habitat: Shorelines of streams, lakes, and rivers throughout North America; very widespread migratory species.
Spotted_Sandpiper.Similar Looking Birds: Solitary Sandpiper bobs but has spotted back and different tail pattern; Common Sandpiper is very similar Eurasian.
Spotted_Sandpiper.Best Ways to Identify: Constant teetering bobbing motion; spotted breast in summer; orange bill with dark tip; stiff shallow wingbeats in flight.

Spotted_Towhee.Description: Large sparrow; male has black hood, white-spotted black back, rufous sides, and white belly; red eye; white corners in tail.
Spotted_Towhee.Behavior: Scratches vigorously in leaf litter with both feet; sings loud 'drink your tea'; dense shrub thicket dweller.
Spotted_Towhee.Habitat: Dense brushy undergrowth, chaparral, and shrubby forest edges of western North America.
Spotted_Towhee.Similar Looking Birds: Eastern Towhee is similar but lacks white spots on back; Rufous-sided Towhee was former combined name.
Spotted_Towhee.Best Ways to Identify: White spots on black back and wings; rufous sides; black hood; red eye; white outer tail corners; ground scratching.
